utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we have the witness, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench? Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Good morning. I would just like to bring -- and ask the Court's permission to be absent from the courtroom today due to the fact that we do not have an interpreter that will be paid by the Registrar and I cannot assist Mr. Stojanovic in anything. From this position, if I could be excused, I could be working on other matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, of course you could be excused. But as for the matter with the interpreter, we consulted with the Registrar, and we were told that the fee for the interpreter is included in the lump sum payments to your team. It's a matter that should be solved between you and your lead counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I would be happy to have it solved between me and my lead counsel. But as it stands right now, Mr. Djukic is not paid for my hour that is he interpreters between counsel, only between myself and Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. If I might be excused, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we start, I apologise for the delay. We do have a list of the exhibits and we can distribute that right now. Again, I apologise. We should have done this before coming to court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start for the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm ready, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And before we start, I would like to remind the parties that Mr. Nikolic is a convicted person by this Chamber but he's also a witness ready to have us to understand the situation that happened in that period. He is entitled to have the same treatment with other witnesses. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nikolic. I take it --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it before coming here today your lawyers advised you of the Rule, Rule 91, regarding the consequences for lying in court. Did they not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my attorneys have informed me of my rights and my duties and the consequences that you mention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of your lawyers is -- in fact is from Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are well aware in the former Yugoslavia the accused had the right to lie in court as part of their defence. They were entitled to do that. From your own experiences, you are aware of that, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, is it not a fact that you were prosecuted back in 1987 with respect to Article 167, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Code, or has that slipped your mind?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not criminally prosecuted, if we are thinking of the same thing. It was an erroneous qualification by the responsible body, and it had to do with a foreign exchange offence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps that's why the records in the police department and the judgement have somehow vanished, yet in the police department, where there's a special register for crimes, you're still registered of having committed a crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I object to the conclusions, the factual conclusions without any factual support of records. We don't know what he's talking about, that they've vanished. I mean, that's not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. If I could at this point in time show the witness what has been marked previously for identification purposes D12/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could please look at it and see if you can identify your name on the document.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can identify it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does this document describe?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know exactly what this is about, and I'm ready to prepare to their -- to explain to Their Honours all the details concerning this document that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, however, demonstrates that you were charged with a criminal offence, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document -- demonstrates that those who submitted charges wanted to suspend me from my duties so that I wouldn't be one of the candidates for the commander of the regional MUP station in Zvornik for which I was a candidate at the time, and this document shows that this is no criminal offence. Actually, this document doesn't show anything. The proceedings that were conducted was completed with the conclusion that this was a foreign exchange offence and Nazif -- I bought from Nazif Muminovic 500 Swiss Francs. I paid him for this. And this document shows nothing more than that. Momir Nikolic was never criminally convicted on the basis of submitted charges. The charges submitted were rejected and what Nikolic was called to account for was for a foreign exchange offence, because in those days the law on foreign currency dealings in the republic in which I lived stipulated that persons who purchase more than 500 German marks or the equivalent of any other foreign exchange are -- is considered an offence. And I bought these 500 Swiss Francs from Nazif Muminovic, which in those days was an offence. The previous law in the former Yugoslavia, Mr. Karnavas, envisaged - that is, the law prior to these charges being submitted against me - stipulated that buying foreign exchange above that sum was an offence, but by decision of Mr. Lazar Mojsov, that law was amended and it was no longer in force and it was not a criminal offence at the time these charges were made against me. And let me mention also, I was not convicted on the basis of the charges made by the MUP of Bratunac, that is, their inspector Muminovic. I wish Their Honours to hear the explanation. Their main aim was for me to be disqualified temporarily. It was not important whether I would be convicted or not. The main purpose was to disqualify me as a candidate for the post of commander of the police for regional traffic, because according to our law, a person who is being charged for a criminal offence could not be considered a candidate for such an appointment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you'd look at that document, sir, does it not state that the -- that the copy of the report on commission of the criminal offence has somehow disappeared? Does it not state that on this document that has been signed by the commander of the police station, Marko Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to interrupt the witness. I asked him a specific question, if he would look at the document and identify -- and tell us whether it states that the file has gone missing. I gave the gentleman plenty of opportunity to give a full explanation. Now I'm asking that he answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I don't think the witness began to answer his question. He just said, "if I remember well." It's the beginning to answer a question. You have to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll wait. I'll exercise some patience. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had started my answer by saying that if I remember well, I think this was a person who came from Hadzici and has nothing to do with Bratunac, nor is he informed about the documents. In this document, he can claim whatever he wants to. But I am claiming that neither I nor my lawyers have anything to do with the disappearance of that document. If it has disappeared, then that's their problem, not mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, no one has accused your lawyers. Let's get that straight. Secondly, last time you were here, on direct examination the Prosecutor went through great pains of talking about stamps affixed to signatures to ensure that there is some sort of an authentification. Could you please look at the document and see whether there is a stamp and whether there is a signature of Marko Davidovic with his job description. Could you please look at the document. Do you see it; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document. I see that it bears a stamp. I see that there's no signature over the stamp. I don't know whether this is the signature of Marko Davidovic, because I don't know what his signature looks like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do see his name and you see a signature and you see a stamp?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see what can be seen on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the top of the page, it demonstrates that this document, at least on its face, comes from the Republika Srpska - right - the Ministry of the Interior, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there not some official numbers there beneath where it says "Public safety centre, Bijeljina Police Station, Bratunac"? Are there not some official numbers there with respect to this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are numbers that I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could go to the second paragraph, the second paragraph, the one that does not start with your name. And if you could look at the last sentence. Does it not say, "However, the case file --" and in brackets it says, or parentheses, "Copy of report on the commission of offence, end of parentheses does not exist in -- as it has disappeared in an unidentified point in time and under unclear circumstances"? Does it not say that, sir; yes, no, maybe? Pick one of them, of the three.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you said is written in that document. But what is your question, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on to the next -- the next segment. Let's talk about your background. Now, as I understand it, you're from the Bratunac area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at one point, I take it you went to the military academy in Zagreb? And left without reason. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not. It is not right that I went to the military academy, because I was only 15. What is correct is that I went to secondary military school in Zagreb; that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So and you left. You did not complete that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school is completed in one year. After the first year, at that school, I moved to the technical school in Bratunac. So I didn't graduate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was: Did you complete the school, the academy there in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that. Now, after that, after graduating from high school, you went to the university college of the National Defence, and that was in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, help me out here. Did you ever get a university degree?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get it from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I graduated in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what was the name of the institution from which you graduated in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The full name is the Faculty of Political Sciences. I studied at the Department for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I had it wrong. So it was the Department of National Defence. All right. And as I understand it, because you were a bright student, you were able to finish early.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I was declared the most successful student in my generation at the Faculty of Political Sciences, studying defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- so I take it you were the number-one student. If you were the most successful, you've got to be the number one.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That need not be so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You were the -- all right. You were the most successful but not necessarily the number-one student. Kind of an oxymoron, but okay, we'll receive that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at that institution -- that's not a military academy, is it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not where one would go to learn basic military -- get a basic military education, as in the academy.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But -- what's not right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not right that you don't go there to acquire basic military knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So let -- help me out here. Are you saying that the institution that you went, you get the same basic military education as one would go -- would get from the military academy? Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So someone who graduates from the academy, would it be fair to say, does get that basic military education, does he not - or she?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say that one acquires basic military knowledge at that faculty --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Or department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, work with me on the military academy for a second. When one graduates that, he qualifies to have a ranking, as I understand it, of lieutenant or first lieutenant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when one graduates the institution or the department, which is, I guess, part of the University of Political Science, he or she does not qualify to get a rank in the military.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He does qualify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... a rank? Is that what your answer is?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not my answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you graduated, you became a high school teacher, which in your country you call "professors"; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were teaching high school boys and girls about the military, some basic information about the military; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were teaching them how to command.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were teaching them --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- How to coordinate, among different units.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or maybe you were teaching them about some -- some special skills, like intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't teach them those things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Why don't you tell us. What exactly are you teaching these boys and girls in a high school with regard to military science? What is it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the secondary school centre Djuro Pucar Stari, I taught the subject called defence and protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that entail? If you could tell us a little bit about it.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't list all the subjects that we covered, the curriculum for the subject of defence and protection, but it is a programme adjusted to children of their age adopted by the pedagogical council of the state at the time. So I'm really unable to list all the topics that were covered over a period of one academic year, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, did you -- everybody had to serve -- every male had to serve in the military in the former Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every military-able man; not everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that correction. And you were an able man; right? You still are, in fact. You certainly were during the period that we've been discussing -- regarding Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was military able.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as a able man, did you attend the military before -- or let me just go one by one. Did you attend the military? Did you do your military service? I think it was 15 months.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did do my military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that before or after your university education?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was before my university studies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you were one of those bright students or bright individuals that they plucked to attend the reserve -- the school for reserve officers.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. They never selected you to become a reserve officer when you were doing your military service.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after teaching, as I understand it - and I might be a little fuzzy on the dates, but help me out here - somewhere around 1984 or 1986, was it, you -- you joined the Territorial Defence? You stopped teaching boys and girls in high school and now you were with a Territorial Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 1986, I moved and started working in the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that before -- that must have been before you joined the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never a member of the SDS party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then I must have it wrong. Now, when you were there, you were working in intelligence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I just wish to add something. I mean the period you're asking me about, 1986. So in 1986, I was not a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Because the storm was coming your way, by the way. Now, at some -- while you were there, in the Territorial Defence in 1986, you were in -- as an intelligence officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the assistant commander for intelligence in the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Help us out here. What exactly does that mean? That's a big title. Help us out.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What would you be interested in?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell me exactly -- well, if you could give us sort of a synopsis of what your job entailed. That may help me ask the next question.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My job as assistant commander for intelligence work means monitoring, detecting, assessing, evaluating the enemy. It also entails work in compiling documents, orders, et cetera. And it prepares intelligence data and information to the commanding officer for him to be able to make his decisions -- the proper decisions and the proper orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could go on talking at length about all that, but I think that is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It helps me out. Was there a particular enemy in that -- in that period of time, 1986, that you were focussing on while you were at the Territorial Defence in Bratunac? Just if you could help us out here.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For the most part, during that period of time it was a case of studying NATO forces and the forces of the Warsaw Pact. They were forces that were studied during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So it would be fair to say that that was sort of a -- an inactive period. There wasn't a whole lot of activity going on that required your intensive intelligence work.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. By the -- so that wasn't a very active period for you, that required you to -- to really hone in your skills as an intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite the opposite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll take it -- I'll move on. I take it, though, that you took this job fairly seriously, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took it the way it should have been taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you go to the Pancevo centre for intelligence and security to get the proper education and training for someone that is going to be doing that sort of work for intelligence and then later on in security? Have you ever heard of the centre?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard of the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, that's a starting point. Now, did you attend it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Pancevo. I wasn't at the centre there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you go to another centre, where they trained -- please listen to my question very carefully. Did you go to some sort of a training centre? And I'm talking about before 1992. Okay, so between 1986 and 1992, did you go to any training centre to get specialised training on intelligence and/or security, during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went to a training centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us, so we can look at the records at some point. What training centre and the time that you went there, the period, if you can recall.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I can. I went to a training centre which was set up at the time in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that educational centre, provisional one, was in a place called Nemila near the town of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how long -- I know the Pancevo centre runs a six-to-nine-month course. How long was your course?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The training lasted seven working days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it after the seven working days you were fairly confident that you knew the craft, the one that's taught at Pancevo for that six-to-nine-month period?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never made the comparison, because I didn't know what Pancevo's programme was and curriculum. I passed through the plan, seven-day-training course in the educational centre in Nemila, and I became acquainted with the basic elements which this seven-day training programme had focussed on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall the year, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an exact year. I think it was immediately after my arrival at the headquarters, but I don't know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I take it one of the things that you were trained on were the rules.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Amongst others. There were excerpts from the basic rules governing intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in -- in 1992, you were appointed by the Crisis Staff, is I recall, the SDS Crisis Staff in Bratunac to become the commander or acting commander of the Territorial Defence in the Bratunac area, because at that point the Drina Corps did not exist yet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So let's walk it through, then. In 1992, you were in Bratunac; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were still with the Territorial Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Engaged in tasks -- what I did was I was assistant commander for intelligence, and I was appointed to that post earlier on in 1986.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. But work with me here. We're going to go step by step. Now, there was a Crisis Staff in Bratunac, was there not, in the Bratunac municipality that was headed, I believe, by one of your own friends, Mr. Deronjic? Was he part of the Crisis Staff at that point, or do I have it wrong?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And it's my understanding- I might be wrong- but it's my understanding that back then the Crisis Staff of the municipality appointed you at some point in 1992 as the acting commander of the Territorial Defence in the Bratunac area.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff never appointed me staff commander, and an order of that kind was never handed to me or conveyed to me. The situation was quite different, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If I may -- maybe I'm getting ahead of myself. Let me just ask the question: Were you ever an acting commander of the Territorial Defence in Bratunac back in 1992; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the acting commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the Territorial Defence is financed, as I understand it - and I might be wrong; help me out here - is financed by the municipality; right? Like, the Zvornik area, they had their own Territorial Defence in the Zvornik area, financed that. In Bratunac, it came out of their budget. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is not correct in whole. In part, yes. But in principle, that was not how the Territorial Defence was financed, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. How did you get this appointment though? Who was it that said, "Momir Nikolic, from this day on you're going to be acting commander. You're going to give orders. You're going to send men into certain areas to retrieve certain equipment that's been captured by the Muslims" -- or so on and so forth. Who gave you that duty? Or did you just wake up one day and say, "Hey, I'm an acting commander," and then just self-designate yourself as one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object to the form of the question. I think fundamentally it's a simple question. But it was so long that unless we do something about that now we will be here forever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas, try to keep your questions as simple as possible. Maybe one sentence will be enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I'll be as laconic as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because this point is not as crucial as you think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It may become at some point, Your Honour. It may become.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who appointed you do that position, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position of commander of the staff of the Territorial Defence or, rather, the acting commander, I was appoint by the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't I ask that question earlier? Didn't I say to you: Was it not in fact the Crisis Staff that appointed you, and you said no? And you said this under oath. Can you give us an explanation what part of my question you did not understand?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand, Mr. McCloskey [sic], because you asked me about 1992. You asked me straight at the beginning what was happening, what was going on. You are putting words into my mouth and saying that that was what happened in 1992 and other things besides. And I don't wish, Mr. Karnavas -- or rather, I wish to answer your questions, Mr. Karnavas. You need explanations, additional ones, and if the Court allows me to give them, what happened at one time, then I'm quite ready to do so. To tell Their Honours when I arrived, how I arrived and so on and so forth. And another thing, Mr. Karnavas: You told me -- or rather, you claimed on several occasions that I issued orders, that I issued instructions with respect to armament, equipment, amassing, that kind of thing. I don't understand what you're talking about, because that's not how it was. But I am ready to answer each of your specific questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, when you were the acting commander of the Bratunac Brigade, is it not in fact -- is it not a fact that you did order for your troops in which 13 got killed and about 40 to 45 were injured to retrieve an armoured transport vehicle which has the initials BRDM to be retrieved which had been captured by the Muslims in an earlier event? Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not. Once again, in your question -- your question contains several subquestions. So you take note that I ordered and then you take note and observe many other things along with that. Now, if the Trial Chamber should allow me to do so, I should like to explain. Who decides on the deployment of the Territorial Defence and issues orders. Your Honours, may I show you a document which shows who the authority is who issues orders during that period of time in 1992? May I be allowed to do so?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, just tell us who made that order. I think that's enough.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That order and generally speaking all orders during that period of time, with respect to the deployment of the units of the Territorial Defence, was issued -- or rather, the decision was made by the War Presidency, and that was based on a decision of the War Presidency and the date was the 13th of April, 1992. That is when he -- they decided to deploy the Territorial Defence units and all decisions were made by the War President, whose president at that time was Miroslav Deronjic. And it is true by virtue of my post, I was a member of that War Presidency and took part in its work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So as a member of the War Presidency and in your capacity as the acting commander of the Territorial Defence back in 1992 - and I think it might be May, but I might be wrong - an order was issued to go and try to recapture a -- an armament that had been lost on a previous occasion where 13 individuals were killed - I have their names - and 40 to 45 were injured; is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The first question on that subject referred to the acting commander of the Bratunac Brigade. The same question is now the acting commander of the Territorial Defence. It may just be a mistake. I just wanted to clarify the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I'll break it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you can break your --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll break it down, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- Break it down one by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Back in that period, you were part of the War Presidency, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also the acting commander -- having been appointed by the Crisis Staff, you were the acting commander of the Territorial Defence for Bratunac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by virtue of my post, the acting commander of the staff. I was a member of the Crisis Staff too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. Exactly. And so a decision was taken in which you were part of that decision-making process, to go and retrieve some equipment, an armoured transport on wheels, a BRDM, that had been lost on a previous occasion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That qualification is absolutely not correct. As I'm hearing the interpretation, what you said is not correct, that the reason the decision was made was the BRDM, which had previously been left somewhere and that the decision was made to take it away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Retrieve it. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But a decision was made nonetheless to go and send four to five armoured transporters and a tank to Sandici to try to retrieve it. Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not a fact either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me fast-forward. Do you recall being transported by ambulance to a psychiatric institution as a result of a beating that you received because you as the commander failed to participate in that campaign and then failed to go and retrieve the bodies of the Serb soldiers, or Serb members of the Territorial Defence that had -- that had on your orders and the Presidency's orders been involved in that campaign? Do you recall that incident, being in the psychiatric institution; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, what is your question? Be specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you recall the beating that you received that resulted you in getting -- in having a nervous breakdown and being transported to a psychiatric institution?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall, Mr. Karnavas, every detail which took place on the 28th and 29th of May, and I am ready to explain before this Court all the details that took place during that period of time, all the details and circumstances surrounding Sandici, the attack by the Muslim forces, the tasks which -- and orders issued at the time and who issued them, and I remember and can tell you with respect to what you're talking about that they were not members of the Territorial Defence or for the most part were not members of the Territorial Defence but they were volunteers. And I am ready to tell you what their basic goal was in entering that place, those volunteers, and all the details and circumstances I am completely prepared to explain them. I'm also prepared, Mr. Karnavas, to explain to Their Honours all the details and circumstances of the physical attack on me after what had happened in Sandici, and I'm also ready to explain to Their Honours that I'm not ashamed to say that I became ill afterwards and went to the hospital and lay in hospital for five -- four or five days in Sabac, at the neuropsychiatric department. I'm not ashamed to say that. And I'm not ashamed to say, Mr. Karnavas, to the Court that I continued my treatment in Belgrade. I was not hospitalised there. However, I'm not ashamed to say that. And I'm ready to explain to Their Honours here and now that during that period of time while I was in Belgrade I worked as a physical labourer in a Naftagas company's facility, where I did physical work during that period of time, I did some painting in order to provide a livelihood for my family, who were refugees in Belgrade. So I'm ready to say all that and state it before this Court here. And I also wish to add that it is no shame, Mr. Karnavas, to become ill, to be ill, to go to hospital, and to receive treatment and recuperate after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Back in -- from June 1 to June 3 of 1992 you were at the Dr. Lazar Lazarevic hospital, as I understand it, psychiatric and neuropsychiatry hospital in Sabac, as you indicated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, Petar -- Petar Uscumlic, that's the translator we later see was the one along with another gentleman by the name of Jovanovic came and picked you up and took you someplace else, to another hospital or health facility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the -- the institute --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petar Uscumlic did not come to fetch me. It is true that a lady came from the Uscumlic family, but Petar himself did not come to get me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And by what I heard, you were away five or six months from Bratunac during this period, while you were convalescing.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was away for four -- five or six months, from the 28th or 29th of May, when all this was happening. And I was away until sometime around the 19th of November, 1992. I think those dates are correct, to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- how did you justify your -- your leave of absence with the Ministry of Defence? Because after all, you were still acting when you -- when you left as a result of the beating and the illness that resulted thereafter. You were still the acting commander of the Territorial Defence of Bratunac. What justification did you put down for your absence while you were in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume you know how absences are justified. During that period of time, I was recuperating, convalescing. And after I came to Bratunac, everybody from Bratunac knew why I had been absent. And, Mr. Karnavas, I never need any special justification, because everything that happened to Mr. Nikolic at that time, that is to say to me, was under the jurisdiction of my physician. He was head of the medical corps, so he personally sent me and he knew what was going on. So I didn't need any justification in written form for the brigade's commander or the ministry. I was listed as being on sick leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And while you were on sick leave, you were working in -- in Belgrade. While officially you were on sick leave, you were -- this is what you communicated to the Ministry of Defence -- you were working doing something other than being on sick leave.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I didn't tell the Ministry of Defence anything myself. What I had to say, I stated in the brigade, when I arrived and reported to the commander, who was on active duty at the time. I reported to him, and I told him what had happened; although, the commander who was there at the time had already been informed of what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, by the time you came back or shortly thereafter, it's my understanding that the Bratunac Brigade had been formed, sometime --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And upon your return, having been previously the acting commander of the Territorial Defence, now you returned and you were assigned to the security and intelligence organ of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't assigned to the security and intelligence organ. I was placed at the disposal -- at their -- I was, until my appointment, at the authority's disposition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point you were given an assignment; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What assignment do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the assignment that placed you in the security and intelligence organ. You just -- or are you saying that you just decided, since you were security before, or intelligence before, you're qualified for the job and you just self-designated yourself? How did it go?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. That's not what I said, nor is it what I think. By order I was appointed to the duty of head of the intelligence and security brigade -- organ in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you were not assigned. You were appointed.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was put in that post conducive to the law, pursuant to the law, as it is done in brigades and the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not saying that there is anything incorrect. I just want to make sure that you were assigned or appointed to that particular position, as the Chief of Intelligence and security in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Karnavas, that is not how it was. In my own language, I was informally assigned and placed at the disposal of someone, taken to an organ and assigned there. But I wasn't assigned to anybody. When you say "assigned," in my language that's what that means, assigned to somebody. And appointed -- but to be appointed by order, that means that the individual or command who was in authority, pursuant to the law to appoint me, officially appointed me by an act and document to that post, to that duty. So that is in precise terms what that means. It wasn't an assignment. It was an appointment by order of the superior command at the proposal of the commander who was commander of the brigade at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So you were appointed to this position by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the organ who was competent to do that at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which organ was that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the exact procedure, who actually signs the document, but I do know who makes the proposal. The commander makes proposals for appointments, but in formal and legal terms, I'm not quite sure who actually signs the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that commander?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say that there are two possibilities. When I arrived, it was Colonel Sipcic, and after that came Lieutenant Colonel Tesic. And I don't want to make a mistake, because it's quite possible that one or the other sent the order -- or rather, the proposal for my appointment. But I'm not quite sure which of the two. Either Colonel Sipcic or Lieutenant Colonel Tesic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sometime in 1995 Colonel Blagojevic is assigned as the commander of the Bratunac Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean as far as you know? You either know it or you don't know it. Was he not there as the commander of the Bratunac Brigade in 1995, say, right around May/June?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Commander, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had he been there? How long had he been there before the attack on Srebrenica, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he came in May, then -- May, June, July, two, two and a half months perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're not quite sure which month he came.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not. I think it was in May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us, how many commanders had this brigade gone through from the time that you joined, which was at its inception, so when it was created back in 1992, to 1995 in May? How many commanders?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. I know that they changed. I really didn't count them. I could count them, but I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why don't you take a -- why don't you make the effort and count them. I mean, if you miss one or two, that's okay. But just give us a ballpark figure.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment for me to think it over, please. Well, let's say five or six. Some came twice. They would go and come back. But I'm really not quite sure. I could give you the names and enumerate them to refresh my memory. So my answer is that in that period, several commanders were appointed to the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reason for having so many commanders? They didn't like Bratunac or was there a particular reason that you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There are several reasons one could mention, but it's really not up to me to give you the reasons for the replacement of commanders, nor am I supposed to know all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did the local authorities, the local political authorities have any contact? Did they work at all with the -- with the brigade? Did they have any special relationship?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did cooperate. But as for a special relationship, I don't know what you mean when you use that term, "special relationship".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who was financing -- who was paying for the regular reservists that were -- well, let me back up. In the Bratunac Brigade, did you have professional soldiers? Serving or did you have part-time reservists or both?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If when you say "professional soldiers" you mean those doing their military service, then in one period of time during the war there was, I think, about a company of young soldiers, as we called them, conscripts. But the rest, if we are talking about soldiers and not the officers, then we mostly had reservists, people who had been mobilised roughly in April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they receiving a salary, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that we did receive a salary, which was received irregularly, and it simply lost all value because of the terrible inflation, so it wasn't worth anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they -- did they have uniforms? Were uniforms provided?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had uniforms. All of them didn't have camouflage uniforms. There were various combinations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Uniforms? Who purchased the uniforms for them?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the purchase of uniforms, that was the responsibility of the logistics organ, so I don't know exactly who provided them and in what way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who paid for them? Let me put it that way. Who paid for the uniforms? Was it not the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly it was the municipality, but I really don't know how the finances were regulated regarding the purchase of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me just ask a broader question. Did not the municipality in some -- in some sense finance either part or the majority of the brigade? Weren't they contributing?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The municipality did contribute to the financing and in providing logistics support for the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say the municipality, somebody has to be running the municipality; right? And I take it these were the same people that you were involved with when you were a member of the War Presidency/acting commander of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you ask me? What was your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... So these were the -- when you say -- when we said "the municipality," the decisions -- somebody was making the decisions in the municipality regarding the contributions, the financial contributions and resource contributions to the brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people that -- that were making those decisions were the same people - not all, but some - that were also members at one point in time of the War Presidency, which you were a member of while you were at the same time the acting commander of the Territorial Defence. No?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not right. It is far more complex, Mr. Karnavas. The question of financing is far more complicated than that. All those people were not the same people that were making the decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did Mr. Deronjic still enjoy a particular sense of power in the community while you were -- during that period of time, the period of 1992 to 1995? Was he not still a fairly powerful member, the head of the SDS, which you were a member of at the time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic in those days was what you just said, a member of the SDS. To what extent he was powerful, I really don't wish nor can assess. I know what my relationship with him was. I don't wish to comment on his power and his status.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you said that in 1992 I was a member of the SDS. You didn't ask me whether I was or not. And I can tell you that in those days I was not a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you become a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally I became a member -- or rather, I joined the SDS in 1996, after leaving or after being demobilised. The reason why I formally signed my accession paper was that at the assembly meeting, deputies, in order to appoint me director of the state company Guber Bratunac, required that I be a member of the SDS, because members of the SDS had the majority in the assembly in those days that was making the decisions. So I did so pro forma in 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So formally -- formally it was 1996, but it was the same SDS party that appointed you back in 1992 as the acting -- acting commander of the Territorial Defence, did it not? I mean, wasn't the SDS in control of the War Presidency, which you were a member of, or became a member of?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Karnavas, whether the SDS party controlled the Presidency. I answered your question and told you that I was appointed by the War Presidency in 1992. Now, whether members of the War Presidency in those days were members of the SDS or not, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you -- you stayed in the position of -- of Chief of Intelligence -- or security and intelligence or intelligence and security in the Bratunac Brigade until you left. And I believe it was 1996 by your own account. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout that time I was head of the intelligence and security organ from the time I was appointed in 1993 until I was demobilised on the 20th of April, 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you shared the responsibility both for security and intelligence during that period, or at least up until the period of Srebrenica in, say, the fall, the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a captain at the time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never went to -- never had any formal officer training either as a reservist or as a -- an academy graduate?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. I did undergo a series of training sessions in the TO staff before the war, and I attended all command staff exercises, which implied acquiring training in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said you were a captain. I take it that comes after being a lieutenant; right? In fact, there are two ranks in lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Inaudible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, there aren't two ranks. There's one rank in each category.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Really? Does that go for general too? The same thing with a colonel? There's only one colonel? There's no such thing as a lieutenant colonel and then a second lieutenant, as is called in the local language, some would say first lieutenant and then lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a correct statement, Mr. Karnavas. Second lieutenant, lieutenant, and then captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, when you joined the Territorial Defence in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We can break right here right now, Your Honour, if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. But I hope when we resume the hearing, you'll speak directly into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise, Your Honour. I'll move.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right before the break, Mr. Nikolic, we were discussing your appointment to the Chief of Security and intelligence of the Bratunac Brigade. And at the time - just to recap - at the time you were appointed, you were -- you were a captain; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understand it- correct me if I'm wrong- that in getting that formal appointment, which would have been recommended by the Drina Corps, it was in fact a gentleman by the name of Tolimir from the Main Staff who actually had to authorise or give his okay to your formal appointment. Does that ring a bell at all?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you just said doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know a gentleman by the name of Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who might that person be, and could you give us his rank and where he comes from?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After being appointed, I learnt that Mr. Tolimir, by rank a major general, and that he was head of the intelligence and security or, rather, assistant commander of the -- in the Main Staff for intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was at the time -- he held that position at the time of your appointment as a captain to that position that you were holding from 1992 to 1995 or 1996 in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I thought at this point rather than continue with your -- your background, whereas I understand after you left you went -- you were working for the Department of Refugees and Displaced Persons; right? After you left the army, the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then as I recall, after that you were appointed as manager for a state-owned enterprise, Kartonaza; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were never -- you never worked for that company, that enterprise?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did work for that company, but not after the Ministry for Refugees and Displaced Persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that before?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I worked in Kartonaza after a position I held in another company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Well, if you don't mind, we'll discuss that later, because I do want to get into a matter of embezzlement of approximately 30.000 Deutschmarks or convertible marks that you've embezzled by providing false -- fake invoices. So if you don't mind, we'll talk about that afterwards and let's focus on for right now the -- your functions in the VRS. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's okay, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't mind going into all these matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it that once you received your appointment as a -- the Chief of Intelligence and Security for the Bratunac Brigade and now that you had a formal brigade, as opposed to a Territorial Defence, you became familiar with the rules.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I used the rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So I -- am I to understand that you had the rules in your office and they were available for you to look at and consult in the event you were unclear as to what your functions were?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that, among other things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in addition to the brigade rules, you had the -- you had rules with respect to intelligence, such as the intelligence support of the armed services manual, and it's dated 1987. Do you ever recall seeing that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with such a heading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I had it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall seeing the rules of services of security organs in the Armed Forces of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia dated 1984, the same year as the brigade rules? Did you ever see this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There has been mention too of brigade rules, generically. In a question now it appears he's referring to some sort of formal brigade rules. These are vague questions, and if -- if that could be cleared up, because I -- I know -- I'm not sure what he's talking about and I don't know if any witness could possibly understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in my view, that first Mr. Karnavas talked about brigade rules, and this time he talked about the rules of the armed forces of the former Yugoslavia. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But you have to put your question in a more clearer way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. And for the record, these are documents that we received from the Prosecution, so they should know which documents I am referring to. But if I could be so kind as to have Madam Usher collect the documents. As the documents are being introduced, Your Honour -- or shown to the witness, I will identify the -- the number for identification purposes, the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you'd look at those documents, Mr. Nikolic, and if you want to leaf through them a little bit. We're going to go through them one by one, at least to identify them, and then we'll get into some substantive articles.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've looked at these documents, and the version I have is in English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I must apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If -- if I may -- I believe -- I believe they're copied. On the other side they should have the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at them very carefully. You might find that you'll recognise -- you also have your own language.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I apologise for not bringing that to your attention earlier, but we're trying to save a few -- a few trees.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it now. Two documents in a language I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's -- for the record, I just want to identify them before we delve in there. So -- okay. Now, if you could look at the JNA brigade rules. Do you see them in front of you? And they've been marked for identification purposes P83 --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have in front of me two rules, and neither of them is the rules of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I have the brigade rules in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, I want to apologise. I take full responsibility for the mix-up here. All right. So you have them. And it's called "Brigade rules for infantry motorised, mountain, alpine, marine, and light brigades," 1984. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be correct to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise. We don't have the brigade rules. We can dig them up out of our file if we -- if you could give us a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. This was a Prosecution exhibit, and we didn't want to, as I said, waste more trees by copying a set of documents, but -- and I do apologise. We should have forewarned the Prosecution. It's -- it's my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, if you provide us the lists -- I must say the list is prepared very neatly, and yesterday that we could, you know, dig up from the files of our, you know, files, documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So there's no need for you to copy all these.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree with you, Your Honour, but we did have quite a bit of copying. My staff was working until 3.00 this morning. So we would at least look smoothly -- you know, look good, if nothing else, you know, during the presentation. But obviously, as I said, I apologise. We'll try to get it right next time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have the -- the rules here in English, and perhaps if the English can be on the ELMO, then everyone would see it and we don't need to have a whole lot of copies. But if counsel is going to go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- into this in detail, it's a good idea to see the -- see the words, understand the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed. We saw it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you -- thank you, Your Honours. Actually, if it's okay with the -- with the Trial Chamber, I was thinking of first having him identify and -- to see whether he recognised all of them, because the rules have to be examined more or less together. So if that is -- if that would be appropriate, I would just like the gentleman to see whether he -- whether in the pile of documents that he has in front of him he -- he sees a document entitled "Intelligence support of armed services manual," dated 1987.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have that rule before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And for the record, that is for identification purposes D14/1. Now, do you see in front of you a document titled "Rules of services of security organs in the Armed Forces of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia" dated 1984? Do you see that document?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please, the exact title of the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The English version, translated, that we've received says "Rules of services -- rules of service of security organs in the Armed Forces of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have those rules in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Again, let me apologise.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I've just been handed aren't those rules either. These are instructions on the methods of work for the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no document in front of you dated [sic] "Rules of services," with a big star on it? And for the -- for the record --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. All I have is "Instructions on the methods and resources of work for security," dating 1986.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may have a moment, Your Honour. If I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your, if we may retrieve the document that we gave the gentleman so we could just look at it for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have that English version that Mr. Karnavas has talked about, but unfortunately the -- we have just noticed the B/C/S version does not appear to be the correct translation, which is what seems to be what the problem is. And so that may be a problem with -- with our discovery. And we'll -- we'll try to get to the bottom of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We can move on and -- all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you have in front of you a services regulations of the SFRJ armed forces of the military police?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Of these four documents, one of which we haven't provided you with the correct translation -- do you recall ever seeing them?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- so in your everyday working experiences, while you were there as the Chief of Intelligence and Security, I take it you used the brigade rules? Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, yes. But for the most part, I didn't actually use the rules in any great detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am acquainted with them, but I didn't use these brigade rules in their entirety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you use the intelligence -- manual on intelligence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I did use them, the intelligence support, dated 1987, and another set of rules as well, which you don't have here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And might you give us the name of those rules so we could try to get them from the Prosecution if they have them.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those rules I think also date to 1987. It is a red small booklet, a manual, and the heading is -- the title is "Intelligence security for operations, combat operations." It's a small red book, manual, which I used. And it was to be found in the library of the headquarters of the Territorial Defence while I worked there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So when you were dealing with -- with intelligence matters, you would make reference to that particular manual and perhaps others, but that's what you made your references to.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, those were the manuals which I had before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what about for security? Did you -- did you refer to any rules or manual for security?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Might I ask if you recall the name of the manual or the name of the rules.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the exact heading was "Rules of the security organs of the armed forces --" well, I don't really know. I can't give you the exact heading. But the subject matter referred to security matters, and I think it was published in 1984.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that's what I've been provided, and I apologise for the mix-up. Now, what about for military police? Did you ever look at any manuals or any rules on the usage of the military police?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've provided you with what we received, and it's titled "Services regulations of SFRJ, armed forces, military police."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the record, this is for identification purposes, D15/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall ever seeing these regulations? And if so, do you know whether these were the regulations that you used?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen these rules, these regulations; amongst them, the one you are referring to. And I did use these regulations and this particular one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you use any other rules or regulations? If you recall.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
