utterances.text: No. They were these rules and regulations mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I take it by 1995, July of 1995, you having been from 1986 onwards in the security sector -- in the intelligence sector of the Territorial Defence, all the way to July 1995 you were still -- that was one of your functions -- I take it at least with those regulations and rules you were very familiar with, dealing with intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, would you put it some other way that would be more characteristic of how you see the picture?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we could say that I was sufficiently informed of the rules relating to intelligence and security for combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And would it be correct for me to assume - I'm going to make an assumption now - so would it be correct for me to assume that your functions as -- in the intelligence organ when you were with the Territorial Defence were relatively the same, if not the same, when you were with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that wouldn't be a good qualification or comparison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you have less responsibility in the intelligence sector in the -- when you were with the Territorial Defence, or would you have more responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of my establishment duties in the Territorial Defence, I would have less responsibility; that is to say, I was responsible only for intelligence matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we're talking only about intelligence now. Now, did you -- did the same rules apply, in other words, if I can assist you here, were there a separate set of rules as to how the intelligence organ operated when you were with the Territorial Defence than when you were with the Bratunac Brigade? Or were the rules the same?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, the rules were the same. But previously I told you that in addition to these rules, the set of rules I have in front of me, intelligence security for the armed forces, that I used another set of rules too, intelligence security for combat operations, which in principle is the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I want to make sure I understand this. All right? Help me out here. When you were with the Territorial Defence and when you were with the Bratunac Brigade, the same rules applied.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, were there a separate set of rules? Aside from -- you know, I understand that there was combat -- there was a combat situation from 1992 onwards, but was there a separate set of rules that were inapplicable?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to that separate set of rules, I really don't know that they existed; that is to say, that there was a separate set of rules that were inapplicable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I would take it that by 1995 you have nine years of experience more or less, on-the-job training, in the intelligence sector.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what about in the security sector? From 1992 -- end of 1992 to July and onwards of 1995, would it be fair to say that by that point you knew, understood, appreciated, and applied the rules with respect to the security organ?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just explain what you mean. The question was rather a lengthy one, and I wasn't able to follow you to the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. After three years of applying those rules or being in that position, being in the position of security - now we're talking security. Forget about intelligence. Now we're talking security - all right? By 1995, the fall of Srebrenica, did you know the rules with respect to the security organ, you know, as they applied to you in your position in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was appointed to the post of head of the intelligence and security organ, onwards, I knew to a significant extent my duties and responsibilities from the competencies of the security organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just to make sure that I understand, by 1995, July, the fall of Srebrenica, what you're saying is you knew the rules with respect to the security organ as they applied to you as a member of the Chief of Intelligence and Security of the Bratunac Brigade. That's your answer.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The next part of the question was: Not just knowing, but you understood the rules; right? There's a difference between knowing them and understanding them; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way. So if you know something, you should also understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it you understood the rules. In other words, you merely couldn't just recite them by heart, assuming that you could do that, but you understood the essence of the rules, what they meant.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I did understand what the rules meant, and all I can tell you is this, to make things clearer, that I could avail myself and use those rules. So I was in a position to use the rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next part of that question, the long one, was whether you appreciated the rules. So you knew, you understood. But appreciated; in other words, you understand the significance of the rules, appreciated the importance of the rules. In 1995, did you appreciate the rules that you claim to have known and understood?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995, I knew what the rules pertained to and regulate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you appreciate them? In other words, understood the value of the rules? Knowing them is one thing; understanding them is another; appreciating them is something totally different. Did you appreciate the rules?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I applied the rules in the extent to which the objective situation allowed me to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, that was the last part of the question. So if you knew, understood, and appreciated, it would be a foregone conclusion, it would be axiomatic, it would follow that you would indeed apply those rules; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how else would you put it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a complex question, Mr. Karnavas, and to discuss a rule now is a little pretentious. It would be pretentious on my part to enter into polemics about them. I can now say that I did have those rules, that I used the rules, that I applied them in the extent to which I should have applied them -- I needed to apply them, and that these rules could have been influenced by the situation in which we found ourselves, the different circumstances and situations. So probably - although, I can't give you a concrete example right now - that there were certain things, certain small details which were in keeping with the rules but not completely so, as prescribed by the rules. I don't exclude such possibilities. They were also possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I agree. It's a complex question. Let's break it down here. I think - and correct me if I'm wrong - I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is asked and answered about six to eight times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas, we could not get your point. You know, if you have a final question, put your final question directly to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've just indicated -- you've just indicated that you applied the rules as you understood them to be, but then you qualified it depending on the situation, that the situation might have influenced the application of the rules.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. That's always understood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, here I'm having some problems understanding exactly what you mean. Are the rules clear; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've indicated you understood the rules; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The rules are made clear in order for someone like you to apply them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the rules are designed in a way so they can be used during a fluid situation such as a combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated that you knew and understood the rules and you appreciated the rules, so I take it the rules were your guiding principles as to how you should or should not behave.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The rules explained what your functions were.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who you were subordinated to.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who your superior was.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was subordinated to you, who was underneath you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no -- there is no security organ -- or rather, there is. I apologise, there is. In the professional sense, there are subordinate organs, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in your capacity -- in your capacity, you were at times able to use resources, staff, such as the military police; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the way you put it is not how it stands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm using the broader sense. We're going to get into the rules. We're going to go into the detail usage of the rules. But for right now is it not a fact in your capacity as Chief of Intelligence and Security at times you had subordinates at your disposal, pursuant to the rules?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly -- and please, I don't want to misunderstand you or misquote you -- what you're saying here today, at no time and nowhere under the rules you have the right to use military police.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the rules as to the deployment of the military police stipulates exactly the method and work of the security organs and defines the authorisations for this, with respect to the military police. And in keeping, or pursuant to those instructions and rules, I had this relationship that I did towards the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely. That's exactly what I'm trying to say. Maybe I'm being inarticulate today. But you had the capacity to have the police subordinated to you at times in order to carry out certain functions related to your work under the rules.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police is not resubordinated or attached to the security organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't say "resubordinated." I said -- let me -- let me rephrase it. Were there times when you could give the military police orders; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that way. I can't give you a yes-or-no answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about a maybe?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in charge -- well, I can't give you a maybe answer either. I'll tell you how things stood. I was in charge in the professional sense of the military police in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You were in charge of them. So that put them under your supervision, authority, control?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. Professionally speaking, being professionally in charge of the military police and police, implies something quite different. And my competencies and authority in that section were equal to the competencies and authority of the head of the arms and services in the unit in which the military police was located. That is what the rule defines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I to understand that you could not order the military police to carry out any activities? And let me give you an example. I'm getting ahead of myself here, but just to help you out. According to your testimony, you, Colonel Beara, Deronjic, I think it was Vasic or someone else - I'm not quite sure - were sitting around on the 13th at the SDS headquarters having a little chat. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I recall your testimony -- and we're going to get into this in great detail. But as I recall it, in general, at that point, while you were there a decision had been made - it's unclear who made that decision - but a decision was made that members of the -- this is according to you -- that members of the military police, of the Bratunac Brigade, would be used to guard the buses of the people. Because in your version of the events, the situation was very tense. There was a security concern for the people of Bratunac on that particular night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the multi-part form of this question. It becomes impossible to answer such a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may respond, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the witness doesn't understand the question, he can certainly, you know, inform me. He doesn't need the assistance of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I think in this situation Mr. Karnavas is laying the background. I haven't heard a question put forward by him yet. Maybe, Mr. Karnavas, it's time for you to directly ask a question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that scenario, as I described it, based on your testimony, you being in the office late at night, 13th of July, Beara, Deronjic, Vasic? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall stating, testifying that a decision was made at that point in time to use, along with others, members of the Bratunac military police? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To use them for what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To guard -- I apologise. To guard the buses of -- containing the people. Because as I understand your testimony, there were not enough people to transport all those buses that night and guard them at the same time. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not how I testified about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So are you saying that in order -- a decision was not made on that night when you were there to use the military police of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no decision. The military police of the Bratunac Brigade had already been used to a great extent for the tasks and assignments that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's your testimony today, under oath. And you've never given a different version on that, that a decision was made to utilise members of the Bratunac military police on that night?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot quote my own words from the testimony. But as far as I can remember, I didn't speak specifically about a decision having been taken that evening, because it would be illogical. The police had already been used. This was the 13th, late at night. And the detainees were in Bratunac already on the 12th in the afternoon, the night of the 12th/13th in the morning, afternoon, and the night of the 13th. So I don't think I said any such thing, at least not in that context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll move on. We'll get to that later on. We'll -- we'll see if I have it wrong. So your testimony here today under oath is that during this period of the fall of Srebrenica and thereafter you never gave any orders on your own to the military police of the Bratunac Brigade. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. You're quoting me as saying something I didn't say. You asked me about the 13th in the evening, and I said that that was not right. That is the interpretation I'm getting. I didn't say in my statement nor am I claiming now that I never told the military police what they should do. If you want me to say I ordered them things, then I accept I did in certain situations order the military police what they should do, but the military police had already been engaged for that assignment. It received instructions from me as to what to do next, how to behave, where to go. That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So aside from the hypothetical that I posed, based on your -- on your testimony, which I may have wrong, you now are saying that throughout that period you were at times giving orders on your own to the military police. I just want a clear, straight answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object. That's a misstatement of the evidence. I think that's a deliberate misstatement, and that's uncalled for and improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think your question has been answered by the witness already. It is quite clear from the transcript the answer to this question, so there's no need to repeat the same question again and again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I to understand, Mr. Nikolic, that you always applied the rules as they were written and as they applied to you? During this period. We're talk about the Srebrenica period. I'm not interested in other periods.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If, Mr. Karnavas, you are referring to the use of the military police that we were just talking about - and I hope that is what you mean - then I can assert that the military police and I acted to implement assignments ordered by the commander and from the chain of command and that we acted in accordance with the rules regarding the engagement of the military police, the rules of service of the military police from 1985.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you always apply the rules as they related to you, with respect to your functions as a -- the head of the security organ of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that in all the situations when I was able to use the rules, except in situations when that was impossible or in situations when I disagreed with the order to engage the military police. And when the order to engage the military police was not in accordance with the duties of the military police, in those situations, when the commander makes a decision, I have no right to refer to the rules or anything else, and there are were such situations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were situations where you were unable to use the rules, with respect to your functions as a member of the security organ? That's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were situations in which the use of the military police was ordered outside the scope of the duties of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not speaking about the military police. I've moved on. I'm talking to you in your capacity as the chief of the security organ, has broader functions than the military police. In your capacity as the chief of the security organ of the Bratunac Brigade, did you always follow the rules? That was the -- that was the question.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes, to the best of my understanding and ability to use them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So if the rules say, for instance -- this is a hypothetical now. If the rules say that you must notify or get permission or be authorised by your commander before you can do -- carry out a certain function, you always - I underscore "always"- applied the rule? Is that -- is that true?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Always, whenever I had the chance to do so, I informed the commander of my involvement. I always did that during three or four war years. When the commander is there, when I had the chance to do that, I informed him about my involvement. But in principle and as a rule, regarding my engagement and the task given to me as the chief of the security and intelligence organs, are given by the commander. It is the commander who gives me orders as to my assignments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that commander would be the Bratunac Brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not -- and that wasn't Popovic, was it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me help you out here. The commander of the Bratunac Brigade during that period was not Popovic. Did you ever hear that name?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear it. Lieutenant Colonel Popovic was not the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric? Was he the commander?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't the commander either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Colonel Jankovic? Was he the commander?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I take it, from listening to your earlier question, the only thing -- the only time when you were not able to follow the rules and inform your commander in advance was when you did not have the opportunity to apply the rules as they should have been applied.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'll slow down a little bit. Earlier I thought you said that you were unable at times to apply the rules or to notify your commander but you would always do so, provided you had the opportunity, if the opportunity presented itself.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Though I considered that they were not tasks within my competencies, I thought I should inform the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. My question to you -- and I -- it's a very narrow issue. As I understand it, you always went by the rules and contacted your commander, except when you were unable to do so because of the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were objectively speaking very few such situations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I thought that was your earlier answer. I just want to make sure that I have that correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could have questions, we might be able to get through this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You know, I think somehow we get your point. But if you have a case at your hands, just put it directly to this witness. We don't have to go around and around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I just want to make sure that I lock the witness into his position and -- but very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But don't confuse everybody, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your testimony, you were issued tasks by Kosoric and Popovic, or Popovic and Kosoric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a certain part I did receive tasks from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also indicated on direct examination that you received tasks or a task from Colonel Jankovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that I was issued a task by Colonel Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it not a fact that you stated that based on the orders or tasks that you were given by Popovic and Kosoric, on one hand, and Jankovic on the other, you went ahead and carried out those tasks? You said that, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I went to carry out those tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that's when you were the coordinator in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as I understand you correctly, as I understood your testimony, when you were tasked you were in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The tasks that you received from Popovic and Kosoric, according to your testimony, were given to you when you were standing in front of the Hotel Fontana, which is in the middle of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understand it, slightly thereafter but basically in the same vicinity, either in or outside the Hotel Fontana, you get tasked by Colonel Jankovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the Hotel Fontana -- I know you've been away from Bratunac for a while, but help me out here. The Hotel Fontana is at a juncture. One way you go to Potocari. If you turn right, you go towards the Bratunac Brigade headquarters; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bratunac headquarters are, what, a two-minute drive?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Potocari is, as I understand it, halfway between Bratunac and Srebrenica, so we're talking about 10 kilometres or maybe 5. I think it's 10, 5 miles.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's 5 or 6 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I understand your testimony- and we can dig it up here later on- but as I understood from listening to you, that after you received the tasks from both Popovic, Kosoric, and Jankovic, you waited around, you hung around, while the VIPs were there in front or in the Hotel Fontana before going off to carry on those orders.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Karnavas, I have the translation that I hung around. I didn't hang around the Fontana Hotel. I waited for the buses to arrive. So there was a period of time when I didn't have anything to do in Potocari. And then after that, I went to Potocari. But I went to Potocari when Colonel Jankovic told me what my tasks were and when he told me that units participating in the Srebrenica operation had received orders as to what their tasks would be in that operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were being sent there to coordinate.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After that, that is to say, since I knew that the units that were there had already received orders as to their role in the operation, I went there to coordinate work in that operation in Potocari, as I testified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, a poor choice of words on my part when I said you "hung around." You waited. You waited before going off to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated that it would have been a two-minute drive for you to leave the Hotel Fontana to go over to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters; right? That's an established fact by you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said that, and I said -- I'm now saying up to five minutes, on the outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll take five. You did not go to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters before heading off to Potocari, did you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't go to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from your testimony, you've never said, at least thus far, that someone told you, Momir Nikolic, "Do not leave the Hotel Fontana premises." In other words, nobody prevented you from getting into your car, which you had as a security officer, the head of the security intelligence, drive down to the brigade and see whether your commander was in and if so, inform him of the orders that you had received from Popovic, Kosoric, and Jankovic. You did not make that -- that trip to the headquarters, did you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you made -- had you made - had - had you made that trip, you might have determined, learned whether your commander was in the headquarters or not if his office; right? Had you made that trip.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had made that trip and if I had looked for him, I would have seen for myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And I guess what I'm trying to get at is you had the time and the opportunity on that particular morning, if indeed -- if indeed you are correct in what you've stated, you've had the time and the opportunity to inform your commander that you had been issued tasks by others who are not your commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't put it quite like that. I could perhaps confirm that I did have time to go to the brigade headquarters, and I can say that my assessment was that there was no need for me to inform Commander Blagojevic about the operation because such a large-scale operation in which Colonel Jankovic had told me that these units had been engaged, it couldn't have happened without decisions of the commanders, ranging from the commander of the Main Staff, of the Drina Corps, and the brigade command. It is quite impossible. And that is why I didn't go to inform him. And anyway, I know that the refugees, the prisoners and concern for them was within my purview. And regarding those tasks defined by the rules of service for the security organ, it is not prescribed that I should keep running over to the commander and ask for his permission for every task. Mr. Karnavas, one could put it this way, that I have the authority from the commander for all the tasks stipulated by the rules of service, according to which the commander must know better and more about those rules than myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me get back to this -- to the earlier part of your answer. You're making an assumption today, are you not, that Colonel Blagojevic knew anything about this operation that Jankovic tasked you. This is an assumption on your part. Is it not a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not assuming anything. I'm convinced that the command structure knew about this operation. That is my conviction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you speak with Colonel Blagojevic that morning about this operation; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me about the 12th in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not discuss that operation on the 12th in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, you had no contact with him on that particular morning.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the operation in Potocari, I did not have specific contact with Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so I make -- just so I can understand your answer, as far as you were concerned under the rules - which we'll get to after the break - as far as you were concerned, you were free to do -- to carry out those orders in Potocari, the orders that were given to you by Popovic, Kosoric, and Jankovic. That came under your authority and you didn't have to inform your commander about it at all.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that, that I didn't have to inform him. I did inform my commander about tasks and my involvement, but I said that that morning I didn't talk to him about the operation and that he did not issue me any orders in connection with the operation, and he couldn't have, because I didn't discuss it with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did not inform him before the fact - not after, but before - in other words, before going to Potocari, before taking the initiative to carry out the orders that were given to you by Jankovic, Popovic, and Kosoric, you went ahead. You didn't talk to the commander; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was a decision that you made.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't a decision that I made. It was an order that I observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were ordered not to -- to meet with Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So the decision not to consult with him, the decision not to take the two- or five-minute drive to headquarters, the decision not to see whether he's in to speak to him was yours and yours only.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was my decision, on the basis of my authority, with respect to prisoners of war and the duties that I was to be engaged in. And, Mr. Karnavas, let me just add: All my responsibilities linked to prisoners, refugees, et cetera, are defined by order of the brigade commander, and that provision and my responsibilities is something I'm well aware of, because I am sufficiently trained to realise and appreciate what my responsibilities are in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This would be an excellent time. We'll cover that next area when we come back, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that this is an important part of the cross-examination, and I'm sorry that you spent a lot of time on those, you know, rules before. So we have to cut it here. I hope after we resume you could be more streamlined and concentrate on those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. This is as streamlined as I can get it. But I will -- I will endeavour. I will endeavour to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. We'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Nikolic, before we -- we go through the various rules -- are you okay? Before we go through the various rules, which unavoidably will take some time, I would like you to please inform us what you believed your functions were and your responsibilities were first as the head of the intelligence organ and then, second, as the head of the security organ. And if you could do it in that order, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. This, too, is a very broad area, but I'll try in the briefest terms to tell you what my duties and responsibilities were as head of the organ for intelligence and security in the light infantry brigade. My basic task and duty in the sphere of intelligence security was to collect, process, and send out intelligence information to the commanders so that on the basis of the intelligence data provided they would be able to make the right decision or issue the right order. Next, my duties would also be to provide military and professional assistance on a continuous basis to subordinate intelligence security organs. In this case, those would be the assistant commanders for intelligence and security matters, in the light infantry brigade. Next, within the framework of the organs which I headed, it was my duty to see to documents as the head of the security and intelligence organ in the Bratunac Brigade, in specific terms, I kept a logbook of the intelligence reporting and was also at the head of a diary, intelligence diary that we kept. This was another document that I oversaw and kept. And then my duties and responsibilities also entailed the decision-making phase; that is to say, to propose and put forward to the commander measures of intelligence security, and also on the basis of the commander's decision, or in exceptional circumstances - and I'm talking about exceptional, extraordinary circumstances - on the basis of the basic concept that the commander had to draw up a plan for intelligence security, and then also after a decision had been taken, once the commander had made his decision, it was my duty to write and compile an order for intelligence security for subordinate units. And for Their Honours, let me explain and expound here. As head of the organ, I would write out and compile the order for intelligence security to the subordinate units or, rather, battalions. However, the order would be signed by the commander. The signature would be the commander's. The commander would review it, authorise it, and then sign it. The case is the same with orders; that is to say, I take part in the writing of orders, orders to reconnaissance units. In the Bratunac Brigade for a time a unit of that kind was set up, a reconnaissance unit. It was in fact on the level of a platoon, and it was also the duty of the intelligence organ to write out and take part in the writing of orders for reconnaissance work to subordinate units or, rather, to the subordinate unit. And in this case, it was the reconnaissance platoon of the Bratunac Brigade. Similarly, I should like to add, in connection with this order, that the order is conceived and written out by the head of the intelligence security organ. However, the order for reconnaissance work, its definite shape, the text and contents of this document, that is something the commander has the final say in and then signs and is then sent down to the subordinate unit or the reconnaissance platoon, in this particular case. Now, I could go on and tell you about the ways in which this is done further down the line, but I don't think that's something that you asked me about. But if you feel like it, I will do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. I take it that's what you understood -- that's what you understand your duties were and that's what you understood - past tense - that your duties were at the time that you were performing them during the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were my duties. They ranged within the frameworks of these responsibilities of mine that I have outlined and were in keeping with the rules governing intelligence security and the rules on intelligence and combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And -- well, you were wearing two different hats while you were working in the Bratunac Brigade as the Chief of Intelligence and Security, because there was a light infantry brigade; is that correct? And by that I mean one for security, one for intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One person embodied and combined the two, intelligence -- the intelligence organ and the security organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact -- but those two positions are distinct and separate. Even though you were carrying them out yourself, those are two different functions, in security and intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You can't put it that way. These two functions are very similar, and there are a series of immediate and further removed links between one and the other function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before coming here today, as I understand it - correct me if I'm wrong - you've spent a considerable amount of time with your lawyers going over the disclosure material as well as the rules. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my lawyers I spent as much time as was necessary, as far as we assessed. And we dealt with all the documents and everything that we had at our disposal, in the sense of preparing the defence well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise. I just think we might be able to clarify something. The question was originally: Describe your intelligence duties and your security duties. The witness did not have a chance to describe his security duties. He did use a term that gets translated as "intelligence security," but that in my belief has to do with his securing of the intelligence information, not to do with the security branch and those duties. So there may have been some confusion on that point. And I don't know if counsel wants to ask him about his security duties. But as far as I know, he didn't -- that was his first question and he didn't get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it depends on you, whether you would like to pursue along this line or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I assumed that the gentleman was mixing the two or combining the two, and that's why I asked whether there were two distinct functions. But I will clarify it, Your Honour. All right. For the record, the gentleman was shaking his head. I take it --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you want to -- do you want -- would you like to have the opportunity to describe to us what your functions were, as you understand them to be, as the head of the security organ?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I answer that question, I should just like to say that Mr. Karnavas asked me separately. He asked me to explain intelligence duties, intelligence work and my duties within that area, and that previously I had been speaking expressly about the intelligence part. So now I would like to say a few words about my role in -- as a function of the security organ. The basic tasks of the security organ in the light infantry brigade were the following: Security for facilities and premises, individuals and property, which if we're dealing with individuals, then they belonged to the light infantry brigade; and then it was also -- as the security organ, it is -- it was my -- I was directly responsible for the professional heading and work of the military police; and to make things quite clear, commanding the platoon of the military police, commanding and leading the military police. That comes under the competence of the commander of the unit or institution within whose composition we have the military police or has been attached to it. In this case, the military police is directly controlled and commanded by the commander of the brigade. Now, what does it mean that my role was the -- that I was directly -- immediately responsible for the professional commanding of the military police platoon? That means in actual fact that I was responsible to see that the military police were ready for combat, combat operations, and that my role was to propose to the commander the best possible ways and means of deploying the military police unit, platoon, in keeping with the rules and regulations governing military police deployment. It was also my job to control the implementation of orders and measures issued by the commander, and then also that the military police platoon should be given all forms of professional aid and assistance in the sense of being able to carry out the orders issued by the commander, and also it was my duty within the frameworks of all this to take care and see that the military police was organised properly and that services were organised which are necessary for a certain assignment to be accomplished. These services - and I can repeat this again so that the laws can be interpreted properly - because of the few people that made up the military police platoon, that is to say, there were just 30 men, that the participation of policemen in certain services of the military police was multiple, multi-fold, which meant that one policeman at one given point in time would take part, for example, in the security service, in providing security. Then he would take part in the patrolling and in other services too. So that was the principle, this multiple principle governing the functioning of the police, and the duties of the head, vis-a-vis their task. And just one more sentence, if I may: As far as my authority and competencies went, linked to the professional control of the military police platoon, these went as follows: They were authorisations by the head of the branches and services in the unit in which the military police platoon was located. The same authority and competencies, to quote an example, were vested in me, when it came to military professional aid, and military assistance to the platoon, just like the head of the traffic service and communications service intended for traffic control, for example -- the military police for traffic control. He sees to the professional training of the department. He sees that the men are equipped properly, and he sees that they are deployed properly, that they are trained professionally. So he sees to that, and that's faired just as I see to the professional aspects in the military police -- engaged in military police functions and tasks. That briefly would be that. So the military police platoon, in addition to these tasks, tasks in providing security for the staffs, headquarters, materiel, and technical means, also engages in military discipline, sees that measures of military discipline are adhered to, and helps uncover crimes and the perpetrators of crimes and offences within the jurisdiction of what the military courts have to deal with. So those are the basic tasks and duties, and my participation there in the military professional sense, to help them carry out their tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let me ask the same question again, and I'll try to be clear. From listening to your description of intelligence and then security, it seems to me that they are two distinct functions, separate. They're separate and distinct.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they are separate in the sense that I have just explained it theoretically. However, they are closely connected. And let me just quote you one example, to make this quite clear to you. On the one hand, you have the detention monitoring of enemy forces, their intentions vis-a-vis your unit; that is the intelligence portion. And on the other hand, from the security job, one of the tasks is to prevent the infiltration of those same enemy forces by making diversion, sabotage, and so on. So in that context, I say they are connected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you were carrying out all of these task, both of those tasks that you -- because both of those fell on your shoulders, as opposed to in a regular brigade. You had two individuals. You were saddled with both those responsibilities and duties, one person, Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the head of that particular body, organ, and I performed those tasks; of course, with assistance by another -- from another individual who was working within that same organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were giving -- you were taking the lead.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the chief of that organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just to be on the safe side, I'd like to go through the -- the rules, the brigade rules, and then the separate rules so we know exactly -- just not all of them but just some of them that may be relevant to your testimony on cross and may shed some light on your testimony on direct. If you could refer to the brigade rules. And I had previously indicated that this was marked for identification purposes as P83, for the record. If you could look at paragraph -- they're numbered -- 118. It talks about the intelligence organ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it, paragraph 118.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And if you could briefly -- if you could quickly look at it.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have had a look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This in -- and I don't want to put words in your mouth. But this in essence characterises in general what the intelligence organ's responsibilities are, which is pretty well what you said earlier -- what you said earlier in your response. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here in paragraph 118 we see set out in principle the professional tasks and defined as to what the intelligence organ actually does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And it's a continuous -- it's a continuous function. In other words, you continually have to be in the field or constantly engaged in the gathering of intelligence and providing the support services to your commander as they are reflected here in paragraph 118; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, what you've just said is not what is written here. It doesn't say that I have to be in the field constantly. And as I understood it, that -- actually, that is not the way in which intelligence data is collected, and that is not what this point or paragraph defines here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't say "in the field," but are you suggesting that you sit in your office and you just wait for the intelligence to come to you? Is that your understanding of what you as the Chief of Intelligence should be doing?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. I don't wish to say that either. But from time to time, I do sit in my office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sure you do. Now, 122 talks about the security organ. Further down the page. And that again, in general, sets out what you're supposed to be doing.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the very last paragraph talks about the expert direction that the security organ gives to the military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that last paragraph does. The security organ provides expert direction for the military police unit, and that's something I talked about a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it also indicates that you make recommendations to the commander. For the more efficient use of the police; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my own language, it is not I who makes recommendations. I propose to the commander the ways in which the military police should be deployed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it if you're going to make proposals, you do that in advance of using the military police, not after the fact.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's quite clear, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It makes sense; right? You don't engage them and then say, "Oh, by the way, commander, I just used the forces in a most efficient manner. Let me tell you how I used them. What do you think? Can I have the approval?"

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I'm following you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I know what you wanted -- what you meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I mean is if you're going to be making proposals, you make them in advance, not after you've already utilised the military police in a manner which you think is the most efficient but you need the commander to give you the authorisation, assuming he -- he agrees with the recommendation.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the commander does not make any proposals. That's what I got from the interpretation. But the commander after my proposal orders the use or deployment of the unit for a specific task and assignment he orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But he -- he has the final authority of saying, "I don't agree with your proposal."

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he does. He does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he can make recommendations on how he thinks, you know, your proposal could be improved; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my proposal, the commander can say that he doesn't agree at all and that he does not accept a single word that I stated. And once the commander, Mr. Karnavas, says "I have decided," that he has decided, then that's definite. That's the last word and there's no more discussion after that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, I'm going to skip ahead a little bit on another topic, but let's cover since we're here on these rules. If I could -- if you could be so kind as to look at Articles 150, 151, and 152. It talks about cooperation in collaboration. And in those articles, it makes references to the term "coordination."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I know that we're taking some time, Your Honour, but I think this is -- I'm laying the groundwork.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the numbers of the paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 150, 151, 152, and in fact you can just skim or read quickly 150 and 151 and zero in, if you will, on 152.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We're told that we don't have that part. So is it possible to put those articles on the ELMO so that we could see what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We can do that. Just for the record, you may -- am I to understand, Your Honour, that we failed to provide you those pages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't mean that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh, okay. I just -- so I could make the adjustments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have those pages either within these rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. [B/C/S spoken] We'll get to them. If I may confer with my colleague, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we had the entire collection, and you can use mine to put on the ELMO, so long as we can all see it. That's fine with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it now, paragraph 151? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah, 150, 151, read those quickly. And then 152, if -- you may wish to look at.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to read it through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Take your time. Well ...

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read out paragraphs 150 and 151.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Why don't you go ahead and read 152 as well, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why don't you go read 152 as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've looked at it and read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we're not going to go into great detail, but would it be fair to say, even though this talks about cooperation and collaboration and it's dealing with the brigade -- and your understanding of what your tasks were as the coordinator on the 13th and 14th of July, is this the basic concept, the basic philosophy, the basic principles of coordination?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Karnavas, as far as I have been able to read in a hurry, this has to do with collaboration during the execution of combat operations. But what I spoke about in my testimony had to do with coordination following the completion of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree. And I'm not trying to -- what I'm trying to establish here, because I haven't been able to look in the rules on coordination after a battle -- so my question is -- my question is: Are the principles of coordination where you have to cooperate and collaborate with all these units, is the principle the same as stated in 151, 152, and 150 -- 150, 151, 152? Just the principles.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not able to draw such conclusions in haste. Coordination in my understanding means unifying in principle of at least two structures when carrying out certain tasks. When I say "at least two structures," or elements, what I mean is, for instance, to be more specific, what was happening in 1995, and that is to unify the activities of members of the Ministry of the Interior and members of the Army of Republika Srpska. But I also wish to say that coordination and these other combat actions were not matters that I analysed. In principle, I do not participate in these things. These are the responsibilities of the chief of staff and the commander, so I'd rather not make -- voice any opinions about it. I've told you what I understand to be coordination, as a measure taken after combat operations. And the same definition could apply under conditions of combat as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me see if I understood your answer. First, the rules that I've showed you talk about combat operation; is that correct? Not post-combat.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These paragraphs, as far as I have been able to see quickly looking through them, relates to what happens in the area of combat operations, collaboration, and cooperation among the various units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that happens at the commander -- the commander is the one that's in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Karnavas, you're asking an unequivocal and unclear question. So could you please define your question clearly, as to what it is you want to hear from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not what I want to hear from you, Mr. Nikolic. I'm trying to decipher your answer. As I understand it, what you're saying is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, in an effort to try to bring some clarity to this discussion, I -- if we could point out that the paragraphs that he's talking about are under the heading in this manual, which is on page 39 of the English, entitled "Work of the brigade command in preparing and organising combat operations." If that could be made clear. I think there's -- appears to be some suggestion that these paragraphs are particular to intelligence and -- and security, and I think we could deal with this document in a proper context, it would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, as I indicated, that I would like you to look at these articles for the purposes of an analogy, unless - unless - and I underscore "unless"- you can point out anywhere in the rules dealing with security or intelligence, a definition of "coordination" which you looked at or could look at or was available to you under the rules at the time when you were assigned in order to be the coordinator of units with commanders of much higher ranking than you. Is there anywhere in any of these rules, anything that would give you some guidance as to the term "coordination"? That you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think I've already answered that question. I understand what "coordination" means. I told you it means unifying at least two structures. I told you that the question of coordination, collaboration, and the other details defined by these rules is something that I did not study. They don't come under the intelligence or security purview. But I can tell you that I was assigned that task at the time and I carried it out on the basis of the order issued to me. I did not delve into that at the time, and I can also say later on I never looked for any reference for the coordination that I performed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Aside from the unifying -- unifying the -- the military with the civilian organ, would it be fair to say that as you understood your task you had to get these different units to cooperate, collaborate, act in unison for a common goal and purpose of which you knew of and were there to assist in coordinating and executing?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey [sic], you've asked me several questions again. But I shall try to answer in general terms what my understanding was of my role. It was as follows: My understanding was that I had to go to Potocari, where certain units had already been deployed and at least two structures, as far as I was informed at the time, that we should work together on the same assignment, that I was designated or, rather, ordered to coordinate because I was from Bratunac and was most familiar with the area, and because this was in the area of responsibility of my unit, according to my understanding, and that I should, among other things, in the execution of that overall operation one of my tasks was to adequately resolve any problems or misunderstandings that might arise in connection with that operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicate it was your area -- it was in the area of responsibility, and you said "of my unit." Is that your security unit, or are you referring to your brigade? What is your unit that you're referring to here?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I apologise for using the term "my unit." When I refer to the unit, I have in mind the 1st Light Infantry Brigade, the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you assumed because this was in the area of Bratunac or where the Bratunac Brigade was operating that it was your responsibility to take care of this -- this incident or this task of coordinating. It fell right within your area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I didn't think anything. I didn't think anything. I simply carried out an order received. I can speak about the zone of intelligence responsibility with competence, and I can speak about the zone of responsibility or area of responsibility of the brigade in general terms. And in my understanding, that was the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade, and that is still my understanding. I may be wrong, but I may not be considered an expert for that area, so that I need not comment on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, based on your understanding at the time and perhaps today - I don't know - was Popovic and Kosoric, one order, and Jankovic, were they authorised to give you direct orders, as you understand the rules?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understood the rules and in view of the position held by Colonel Jankovic - so I'm answering your first question first - his arrival to the Bratunac Brigade and his visit in my office and his contacts and presence there created the conviction that he was a man from the Main Staff who can give me orders as to what I should do when it comes to the prisoners, the refugees, because generally speaking and as a rule I knew and was aware even before receiving the order that concern for the refugees and the prisoners, their assembly, their securing and transportation, was within the competence of the intelligence and security organ.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same with respect to your second question. That was the same understanding I had with regard to Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, who was in the Drina Corps and Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric, who was Assistant Chief of Staff in the Intelligence Department of the Drina Corps. So I had the same view of both of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so I'm clear, the Drina Corps is above the Bratunac Brigade, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the superior command to, among others, the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And of course, the Main Staff is even higher to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from your answer, would I be safe in assuming that your understanding of the rules are that since somebody from above, the Main Staff or the Drina Corps, is giving you an order, one, they have the right to do that under the rules? Is that my -- is that your -- am I correct that that is your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally you're not right, and that was not the explanation I gave. You are not right when you say that automatically, if I understand you correctly, that simply because someone is from the Main Staff that, he can give me orders. That was my understanding of what you said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk about Colonel Jankovic and your answer with respect to Colonel Jankovic. One day he shows up in your office.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your office is, if we're looking at the -- at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, the Kaolin factory, your office would be on the left side, as you walk through the gate, right, second floor?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you've described it correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- the commander's office is on the right side, second floor.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At quite the opposite end. At one end is my office, and at the other end the commander's, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in between there are walls to prevent you from going directly from your office - in other words, walking down the corridor - to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have to go downstairs to the first floor or -- I guess in Europe they call it the ground floor -- all the way -- go out, go through a separate set of stairs in order to see your commander; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now,-- and we'll get to the layout in greater detail later on. But in any event, one day out of the blue, out of nowhere, Colonel Jankovic of the Main Staff shows up in your office and says, "I'm here to stay, to take -- to use your office"; right? Or words to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite like that, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understood it, it was -- what you said, he didn't come by chance nor in the way that you described.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. He shows up though all of a sudden, didn't he? Out of nowhere he just shows up.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I must underline the interpretation I'm getting is that showed up from nowhere. That is not true. Colonel Jankovic came and introduced himself as an officer from the Intelligence Department of the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So he showed up from the main office one day. And what I'm trying to say is he didn't call you in advance and say, "Captain Momir Nikolic, may I have permission to use your office while I'm in Bratunac." He just showed up unannounced.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Karnavas, you've asked me several questions and asserted several things. I said that Colonel Jankovic came from the Main Staff, he came to my office, he introduced himself to me, and he said that in the ensuing period following orders from the Main Staff he would be engaged in Bratunac and that he would be staying and sharing my office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely. He didn't ask you if he could use your office. He was telling you that he's going to be using your office pursuant to orders from a higher authority.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, in my understanding this was absolutely normal procedure. It was a normal act. And officers from the Main Staff or the superior Command never ask officers in a command whether they can come to the unit or not. He could have ordered me to give my office to him, that that was the decision of the commander of the Main Staff. He could have ordered me to move to another office. He could have done that too, told me to vacate it simply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. And based on your understanding and from your earlier answer, it was also your understanding that he could give you a direct order. Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I felt that Colonel Jankovic could give me an order in line with the law on security of intelligence and the rules defined in that manual. One of the tasks that I was assigned by Colonel Jankovic was the task which already had been defined and the participants designated on the part of the command, and my tasks mainly had to do with refugees and prisoners, that is, able-bodied men that we had separated in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so I'm clear, what law on security of intelligence are you referring to? Or was there a misunderstanding by the interpreters? Did you mean to say law on security or law on intelligence? If I could have that point clarified.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have misspoken, or maybe it wasn't interpreted properly. I'm referring to the rules of service that we reviewed a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is that the service for security or is that the service -- is that the rules for intelligence? Because you mentioned both, and I'm a little confused here. Help me out.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can look it up and tell you. One of the rules of service defines the attitude or behaviour towards refugees and prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, are we breaking -- if I may ask a question. Are we breaking at 1.30?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you feel that, you know, you've finished, you know, certain parts of the cross, we could break now. But normally we'll break at 1.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh, 1.45. I can go. I can go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, why don't you take a look at the rules, because I was going to get to that next. I have some rules in mind.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, I'm talking about the rules governing the military police. And among other thing, it says that the military police can take part in securing prisoners of war in camps for prisoners of war, that it participates in guiding the movement of refugees and detects enemy formations. That is one of the tasks. And previously I also tried to explain that with respect to prisoners of war, and in view of the training I underwent, I knew that orders of the commander or of unit commanders define the duties of the security, that is, intelligence organ, with respect to refugees and prisoners. So I think that that is quite a legal and legitimate requirement and task within my jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
