utterances.text: Okay. Let's back up a little bit, because we need to clarify the record. If you could please identify for the record the title of the document that you were just referring to, just the title.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The rules of service of the armed forces," 1985.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the intelligence? Is that what we're looking at? Or the security? I didn't pick that up. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Rules of service of the military police." Now, may I just take a look subsequently at another rule or, rather, both rules to find the section which relates to what I've just been saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to perhaps assist the record, the military police rules have been marked as D15/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could also note for the record that it was Article 25 of paragraph 25(H) where the gentleman referred to the military police taking part in providing security for prisoners of -- of war in camps for prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what you were referring to; right, Mr. Nikolic? Am I correct? When you ...?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did speak about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the nearest military camp vis-a-vis Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that a classical camp of the type that you envisage was in Batkovici. However, what can be in my opinion applied to in the context of this particular point is what was happening in Potocari, that is to say, linked to the prisoners of war, civilians or, rather, refugees. And it can also be taken to apply to provisional detainment in the complex of Bratunac that I spoke about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, if I understand you correctly, when you were identifying, as you claim you did, places where the Muslim men were going to be detained, such as, I believe you mentioned the Vuk Karadzic School, your understanding was that you were -- that you were identifying a camp for prisoners of war; is that -- am I correct? Is that your interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, Mr. Karnavas, that is not my interpretation. I know exactly what those facilities were, and I differentiate between camps and places for provisional detention of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's get back to my earlier question regarding Jankovic, because I had asked you a pretty specific question. Was it your understanding of the rules, the ones that you knew, understood, appreciated, and applied, that Jankovic, being that he was from the Main Staff, a higher-ranking officer, such as a colonel, could directly order you, Momir Nikolic, a captain in the Bratunac Brigade? Was that your understanding back then and is that your understanding here today?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The issuing of orders by Colonel Jankovic I understood as I did all other orders which were issued and were present in other periods of time. So this wasn't any special period of time, that is to say, that orders of that kind were issued just then and there. In my view, in my assessment, both then and now, those are the military professional tasks which were defined in -- as duties of the security and intelligence organ. And if they come from individuals who are from the Superior Command of that particular organ, then I never asked myself the question as to whether he had the right to issue that order to me or not. I never questioned it. So at the time, this relationship and type of communication was quite normal to me, and the goal -- or rather, the aim of respecting that order was that the operation should be executed as the orders stipulated and within the time stipulated. That would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it if I were to look into the rules, I would be able to find somewhere where someone like Colonel Jankovic from the Main Staff, albeit the security sector, could give you a direct order bypassing the Drina Corps, bypassing the commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's a misstatement of the facts, Your Honour. I believe that Colonel Jankovic has always been a member of the intelligence branch. And I -- it's late. I can tell people are getting a little tired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Intelligence. Pick your choice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's your understanding that as someone from the Main Staff, Colonel Jankovic, under the rules now - I'm not talking about in practice - is it your understanding -- if I were to look into the rule, would I be able to find a particular rule that an intelligence officer from the Main Staff can bypass the corps and the brigade commander and go directly to you, who shared this position of intelligence and security and give you a direct order? Will I find this in the rules? And it's a simple yes-or-no answer. If you're not sure, go with maybe. I'll take that as well.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the question wasn't a simple one, and I can't give you a yes-or-no answer, because if I knew everything that happened up until the issuance of that order to me, then I could give you a yes-or-no answer. However, I do not know under what conditions and circumstances, I don't know from whom Colonel Jankovic received his orders or whether he did receive any orders at all, so I don't know many of the facts that went before Colonel Jankovic issued me an order of that kind. All I can do is assume and speculate, surmise and conjecture how he came to issue that order to me, and I don't want to speak about that because, as I say, I don't know what went before, what preceded it, preceded the issuance of the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you could have asked him; right? That's one possibility. "What gives you the right, Colonel Jankovic, to order me, someone from the Main Staff? Where is it in the rule that is says that you can bypass my commander and give me a direct order?" You could have asked him that; right? I'm not saying you would have, because obviously you didn't. But you could have.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, there are some things which theoretically speaking exist or are a theoretical possibility. There is the possibility of things happening the way you said, that is to say, that I could have told Colonel Jankovic -- asked Colonel Jankovic who he had received his orders from. But I don't think that is standard practice or that things are done in that particular wail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not a polite way to treat a colonel, right, from the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not that it isn't polite to treat a colonel that way from the Main Staff, a colonel from the Main Staff, but there is standard practice, standard methods, a mark of respect for one's superior and for one's superior command. So for those reasons alone it would be improper for me to check out Colonel Jankovic and quiz him about who had issued these orders to him, which meeting he attended, whether he called upon my own command, and so on. That's not the way things are done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe not a good idea to question Colonel Jankovic. What about going to Colonel Blagojevic, your own commander? Certainly that's not an impolite approach.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We've spent good deal on that subject at this particular time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I agree with you. Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you've put this question to this witness already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to Kosoric and Popovic or Popovic and Kosoric -- I guess Popovic is security; Kosoric is intelligence. You're wearing both hats. They give you a direct order. You never communicate what was told to you by them at the time to your -- your commander. You go off to execute that order. Question: If I check the rules, will I find anywhere - anywhere - in the rules something that would give us the impression that those two, Popovic and Kosoric, had the right to give you, Momir Nikolic, in your position a direct order bypassing - and I underscore "bypassing"- your commander? Will I find this rule anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. And this is a hypothetical not based on facts, as they've been laid out. And it's also multi-part and confusing. The points are well taken. And if they can be asked in a manner that can be understood, I certainly have no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I apologise if Mr. McCloskey doesn't understand the question which is obviously fairly simple. The witness has not indicated that he does not understand the question. Also, the question relates to early information that he has given. I'm merely asking can he point out -- can he point out to a particular rule somewhere, either in the brigade rules, the intelligence, the security, anywhere - anywhere - that would say that someone like Popovic and Kosoric would give him in his position a direct order bypassing his commander. Can he do that? And if he needs more time, we can -- he can do that during the lunch break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I can respond to your question in this way: I can - and there is an order here - I can tell you that in the order by the corps commander on combat operations and their implementation, the heads of security are directly held responsible for the conduct -- for their conduct with prisoners of war and others. I hope that that order was done in keeping as it was signed by the corps commander, that it was compiled in conformity with positive rules relating to the planning of combat operations, and analogously to that, if the order contains -- if Popovic and Kosoric are made responsible for the prisoners of war, then in the area linked to prisoners of war, in that section, which relates to Potocari in this particular case, then in my view that reference defining the authority of Kosoric and Popovic, to give me instructions as to what I should do with those prisoners of war for which they are responsible by virtue of the commander and his orders. And you have that order in your documents, in your files, Mr. Karnavas. And it is a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And I take it you would not object if we went through the orders after we take our break, our lunch break; right? You would not object to us going through the orders.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have nothing to object. I leave it to the Court's discretion. Anything that the Court rules, I shall abide by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we specifically just identify the order he's talking about for the record. I think he has a specific order in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please, so we could prepare.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is the question directed to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Very well, Your Honour. I believe the gentleman was referring to the Drina Corps order of 2 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With your permission, I can take a look at that order during the break, and then I will specify. Because I can't remember the dates offhand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course. I totally agree. And also, might you be so kind -- might you be so kind to also look at the order that was prepared by your own commander as a result of the Drina Corps order. And that's of 5 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record -- for the record, with the Court's indulgence for one second, I'm referring to -- if he could provide the documents to Madam Clerk -- to Madam Registrar, sorry, D16/1 [Realtime transcript read in error "D61"]. That would be the command of the Drina Corps order for active combat activities dated 2 July 1995 and the Bratunac Brigade command order for active combat action -- that's 5 July, 1995. And for the record, that's marked for identification as D17/1. And so we will provide that to the witness, Your Honour. And these are the orders that I believe that the gentleman was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll resume at 3.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.49 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Good afternoon, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right before we broke off for lunch, we agreed that we would go over the orders of the -- of the Drina Corps and then of the Bratunac Brigade. Now, if we could go first to the -- the Drina Corps order dated 2 July 1995. And again, for identification purposes, is marked as D16/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I should note that on the transcript it says D61. It was probably -- it's an error perhaps because I was not annunciating clearly for the -- whoever is writing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look at that particular order, sir. Just take your time, look it through. When you're ready, let us know.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've taken a look at the document -- or rather, the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've seen it before, I take it, before coming here today?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask, did you see it before coming to The Hague, that is, when you were back in 1995 did you recall seeing it then, or was it -- did you see it for the first time when you went over this and all the other disclosure material with your lawyers?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it first when I received it -- when I received the material from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So prior to seeing it from the Prosecution, you had not seen this piece of document, this order from the Drina Corps of 2 July 1995 when you were the chief of the intelligence security organ of the Bratunac Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not see this order, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "personally," I just want to make sure I understand there's -- you just -- you don't recall seeing the order?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I don't recall whether I saw it or not. I know for certain that this order as it now stands, as I see it here and now in front of me, was not possible. Rather, I didn't have the opportunity of seeing it, because it wasn't addressed to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, just to make sure I understand. Earlier, before we broke for lunch, you had indicated - because we were speaking about, I believe, where the prisoners were going to be detained or what would happen with the prisoners of war as a result of the battle plan on the attack of Srebrenica, and you had indicated that you -- that you were acting pursuant to an order from the Drina Corps. Might you have been mistaken?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I remember, I didn't say at all that I acted pursuant to an order from the Drina Corps. What I said was that in this order is the point of reference in law for the questions that you asked me about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I stand corrected. Now, let me see if I have it -- if I have it right. The Drina Corps issued an order dated July 2nd, the one that you have in front of you that's already been premarked for identification purposes as D16/1. You will see that on the right-hand side of the top of the page it refers to Krivaja 1995. You're familiar with that term, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with the name Krivaja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is it not in fact true that this particular order was drafted pursuant to a directive that came from the Supreme Command, none other than President Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say now is -- actually, all I can do is guess. If I were to take up the directive and have a look at it now, I could give you my personal opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll -- we'll get to that later, if it's necessary. But if I could show you now what has been premarked for identification purposes as D17/1. It's the Bratunac Brigade command order for active combat actions dated 5 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record, I need to clarify a couple of matters. One, this document we received from the OTP in one of the -- the CDs; secondly, the ERN number, for some reason we have not been able to find it in our search and in printing this order out, although we have spent the last three days searching for it; third, the order itself had not been translated, and so we, that is, the Blagojevic Defence team, translated it through our translator, who is an official translator but not employed as an official translator with the ICTY. So the translation that we are providing was done by the Defence, and of course I would take it the next step would be if indeed this document is tendered, which I intend to tender it, then it could be checked and perhaps given the -- checked for the translation by the -- the official department here with the Registry. So with that, if there are no objections - and I see none from the Prosecution or they have this very serious look on their face - okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, if you could kindly look at this document. And see if you can identify it.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you give me a moment for me to take a look at the document first, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've taken a look at the document, the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could -- if you could be so kind as to flip to the very last page of the document. It shows that it's been signed by Vidoje Blagojevic, the commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to what I can see, that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the very first page, again on the right-hand side we see the term "Krivaja 1995."

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from your knowledge and expertise, being in the intelligence and security organ and having been a member of the Bratunac Brigade for several years, by looking at this particular document would it be fair to say that this document here generated by the -- by Commander Blagojevic was generated as a result of the previous order shown to you from the Drina Corps that's signed by General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this first point in the order for active combat actions, I'm able to say that this in general terms was a document compiled on the basis of a previous order, or rather, an order by the Drina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can we be a little more specific? I showed you one document. It's an order from the Drina Corps. If you could look at that document and then look at the one that I've shown you from the -- the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. Is not the order from the brigade the result of the order issued by the higher authorities, that is, the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, probably that is as you say, but for me to be able to judge this document I would need to analyse everything that the first document contains, all the paragraphs, to analyse what is written in the order for active combat action in this document and then to give you a very precise answer. To do so hastily on the basis of a cursory review, I have already noticed that this order was obviously written without me and my participation, because in this order, if I have looked at it properly, I have noticed straight away that there is a certain lack of understanding and imprecise assignment of tasks with respect to the security of combat operations, so that regarding the intelligence security something is written that should not be there, and intelligence security as a measure of combat security does not exist in this document. I may be wrong, but I don't see it. And in a -- an order written by a commander that I was involved in, that never happened and I attended numerous exercises and participated in the drafting of countless such orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me take it one at a time. Am I to believe, or are we to believe that you have never seen this order before me showing it to you today?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say with certainty, but only on the basis of what I see on the last page of this order, that this order was typed in six copies and that it was delivered to the following bodies: An original to the brigade archives, and then to the commands of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Infantry Battalions - that makes it five - and to the chief of staff of the brigade the sixth copy. On that basis, I can assert that this order for active combat action was not delivered to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The chief -- the Chief of Security is directly subordinate to the -- the commander in the brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when it comes to intelligence - and I may be wrong here - but when it comes to intelligence, is it not the chief of staff that actually oversees the intelligence sector? Help me out here.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intelligence and security organ in a light infantry brigade is an organ that is directly linked to the brigade commander, is in direct communication with him. In infantry brigades and other types of brigades, when the intelligence is separated from the security function, the Chief of Security is in direct communication with the brigade commander and the assistant chief for intelligence affairs is in direct communication with the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I or, rather, my person combined both functions at the time while I was performing those duties I was in direct communication with the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I -- if I understand you correctly, one, this document was never shown to you by your own lawyers when it was -- which they would have received through the Prosecution during the disclosure process. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that now. I assume that a document of this kind may have been among the documents, but I didn't pay any attention to it. I don't have it just now on me, but I can check whether I have it among the documents in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall ever discussing an order by the Bratunac Brigade commander for the attack on Srebrenica with your lawyers during the, what, one-year-plus period that they've been working with you? Do you recall them -- do you recall going over a document with them in order for them to analyse what your functions were prior to and perhaps subsequent to the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, with my lawyers I discussed on numerous occasions the overall Srebrenica operation. Not only did I discuss it with them, my lawyers, but I also had occasion to discuss my role, my functional duty, my obligations, my rights and duties, omissions, and every other aspect of my role with a military expert in this area who was engaged by my lawyers upon my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we have that name, if it's okay with you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't mind at all. The expert who visited me in the Detention Unit is Colonel Vuga, from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. Now, I take it -- I take it in discussing what your duties and functions were on the attack and subsequent to the attack of Srebrenica, this particular expert would have had to have looked at orders that were given to you. Or did he just ask you what you thought your duties were and from there he gave an opinion?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, my expert had at its disposal the complete documentation that I had, and it relates to the area in which I was. So every document that my defence team received from the Prosecution was placed at the disposal of my military expert for his analysis. The preparations lasted quite a long time, and after those preparations and after all the documents that I had at my disposal being analysed, Mr. Vuga came to the Detention Unit and that is when we discussed a whole series of issues but from the standpoint of my functional duty as chief of the intelligence and security organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- when you were conferring with this expert - and I believe it was sometime around February or March, as I recall - do you recall ever going over this particular document with him, that is, the order that the commander of the Bratunac Brigade had drafted, an order which would have included your functions, duties, and responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that question. All the documents in my possession and which he as an expert thought should be discussed were discussed. I cannot recall now. There really was a host of documents, and I cannot claim that we discussed this or that particular document. All the documents that my expert thought were relevant and substantive were reviewed by us when he visited me in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Might I ask what did you think -- what did you think your duties and responsibilities were as the Chief of Intelligence and Security prior to, that is, leading up to, during, and immediately subsequent to the fall of Srebrenica? Did you have a clear picture of what you were supposed to be doing? And if so, how?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey [sic], it was not up to me to think what my duties were. I knew exactly what my duties were as the Chief of Security and also as the Chief for Intelligence Affairs. And all I can say is that the duties of my position are quite clearly defined in the rules. On the work of intelligence and security organs. During the immediate threat of war, during the war itself, and my duties within the framework of a particular assignment are defined by order, or pursuant to an order. And they can be seen here. They are visible, from every order. That is, what my basic duties are can be seen from the orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's talk concretely, then, and length go to the order from the Drina Corps, which according to your testimony you've never seen prior to your arrival at The Hague. And if you could look at - and I'm referring to, for the record, this is -- for identification purposes, it has been marked as D16/1. If you could look at and see whether there's a section in the order itself - it's on page 4 at the bottom in the English version, but I -- I'm afraid I don't read Srpski, B/C/S as its known here. There is a particular section with respect to the duties and responsibilities that are being ordered to the Bratunac Brigade. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the page number, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's page 4 in English, but it would be -- it would be under paragraph 5. So if you go to paragraph number 5, and I think it's -- you'll see the -- the section. So that would be on page 3, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- Would it be possible to have this document on the ELMO so that it can be publicly viewed as well if it's going to be a matter of discussion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, maybe you could read the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- Sentence in the beginning of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On paragraph 5, on page 3 it begins "Tasks of the units for separating and reducing the enclave in size." Then on page 4, at the bottom of page 4 in English --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, would you be kind enough to repeat what you just read out. On page 3 ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 3, it was the very first -- the very first sentence under number -- paragraph 5, "Tasks of the units for separating and reducing the enclave in size."

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say that in my version. What it says in my copy is "Tasks: To smash the enemy along the axis of attack, to separate the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica, and reach the line Alibegovac, Vuc Gora [phoen]."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could just interrupt you for a second. Look at page 2. All right? Now, at the bottom of the page number 5, even in my -- even though I don't speak the language and can't even read it, I know that's what I'm referring to. Would that be correct? "Tasks of the units for separating and reducing the enclave in size." Okay?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you would continue on, you should see a section that refers to the Bratunac Brigade. And in fact, I believe it's the middle of the page. Page, of page 3.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade with a part of its forces in direct contact with --" I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please read that section. And we can have it on the ELMO if the public wishes to see it. But from reading that, does it not seem to indicate that this order is giving a particular task to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, will you allow me to read this first --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Before I answer?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I could repeat my question. Does that paragraph that you just read from this particular order, does it not give the Bratunac Brigade a specific task?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of what is written here, the Bratunac Brigade is being given a specific task. But I just wish to say that that was the purpose of writing an order or command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You didn't participate in drafting this, because you've never seen it before coming to The Hague; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you earlier on that I did not participate in writing this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't finished. I haven't finished my answer. But according to the -- all the rules, I should have taken part in writing the first paragraph of this order, that is, I should have proposed the first paragraph of this order to the commander, that is, to provide a draft, and within the framework of combat security I should have proposed to the commander intelligence security as an aspect of combat security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And possibly also - and I apologise - the engagement of a military police platoon, if the commander had decided to use that platoon during combat action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's clarify a couple of points. First of all, the order that we're going over right now was an order that is signed by General Zivanovic, the commander of the Drina Corps. Surely - surely - you're not suggesting that General Zivanovic should have allowed you, Momir Nikolic of the Bratunac Brigade to participate in or to draft a particular paragraph in his order that is based on a higher order from the Main Staff. That's not what you're trying to suggest, is it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Karnavas, that you have completely misunderstood what I was saying. I never said anything like that. I said that in drafting the order of the brigade commander for combat action I should participate in drafting the first paragraph, that is, making a draft for the commander, the contents of the first paragraph, and that I should have within the framework of the drafting of the paragraph of the order linked to combat security there should have been a paragraph on intelligence security and another paragraph on security of combat. That is what I should have been involved in in writing the order of the brigade commander, not the corps commander. And if you're interested in my involvement in writing orders of the corps commander, I can explain that too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, that won't be necessary. I totally agree with your answer. When it comes to the brigade order -- when it comes to the brigade order, the rules are very clear, that you're supposed to participate in those. But I misunderstood you, because I'm still working on the order from the -- from the corps. Okay? Now, if you could -- if I could please focus your attention to paragraph number 10. It speaks of combat security. And if you could look at B, subsection B, where it says "Security." In the English version, it would be on page 7. On your version, it would be on -- it would start on page 4 and go into page 5. But probably the section that you're most interested in, as we all are, is on page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just for clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're talking about the corps order now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The corps order. I've always been talking about the corps order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. There's been a little misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we should put page 6 on the ELMO instead of 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, page 7, Your Honour, is the pertinent part. And if I could help the gentleman out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you will see under section B, called "Security," it says: "The security organ and military police will indicate the areas for gathering and securing prisoners of war and war booty." And I believe that's what you were referring to prior to the break. Did you see that section?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then subsequent to that, it's quite clear. It says: "In dealing with prisoners of war and the civilian population behave in every way in accordance with the Geneva Convention." That's what this particular order says.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could turn now to the order from the Bratunac Brigade, which you have indicated you did not participate in or your contributions with respect to security matters were not taken into consideration prior to the drafting and distributing the particular order. For the record --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That is a misstatement of what he's said on that, and the witness would have a chance to read this document carefully. I believe what he said is he didn't see the section on security that would -- he would normally expect to see in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I dis --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You know, we can play hide and seek here F we want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, just draw our attention to the relevant paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, previously you've had a chance to look at this document, have you not, the one from the Bratunac Brigade? Just now. A few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, am I mistaken -- am I mistaken, but have you not indicated that you did not participate in the drafting the section with respect to the security organ as you normally would be expected to do as is required or you're entitled to do under the rules?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I answer this question, I should like to ask you kindly for Mr. Karnavas to allow me to answer the question he puts to me, because he asks one question after another without me having the time to hear it. So to make our work proceed more smoothly, I'm ready to answer every question but I need time to hear the question and to familiarise myself with the document, because a moment ago there was confusion between these two orders. So please let us move slowly. I'm ready to stay and answer your questions for as long as the Court decides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And may I make another request? And that is please put one question at a time. Very often there are three or four questions in one, and I am unable to follow and to give you concrete answers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Please -- please look at the document dated 5 July 1995 if the 1st Bratunac -- from the Bratunac Brigade Light Infantry Brigade. Could you please look at it.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've had a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please look at paragraph 5.6.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it. I've found point 5 -- or rather, paragraph 5.6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this paragraph not refer to the military police platoon?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it says here -- it says "Reserve: Military police platoon. Have it in the area of the command post of the 1st KM 1, 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, ready to deploy if need be." As it stands, this refers to the military police platoon of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. It also designates what their function is going to be, does it not, at least with respect to this particular order -- well, -- while this order is in effect?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, on the basis of an assignment defined in this way, apart from the fact that the military police platoon should be in reserve, nothing more than that can be seen from this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely the point. What I'm trying to get at from you is from reading 5.6, it designates that the function of the military police platoon while this order is -- is in -- is functioning, is in use, the military police platoon are in reserve. That's the reserve for the Bratunac Brigade. That's their function. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're not at all correct, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So are you saying that Colonel Blagojevic through his order did not put the military police platoon to be the reserve during this order, while this order was being implemented, that they were not in reserve and that they were not supposed to be in the area of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade command post, which would be in Bratunac? Does this not say this?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, that's what it says in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But all I can say -- or I can just say one thing in that regard, that had I taken part in the compiling of this order it would never state that the military police platoon should be placed in reserve, because in an operation of this nature there are so many military police assignments and tasks which should be done that I can give you my own personal opinion. This is not a suitable order and I would have opposed it, quite certainly. And I'd like to propose to the brigade commander that the military police platoon be engaged and deployed on military police matters within the frameworks of the operation and after it. With an order of this kind, with an assignment to the military police of this kind, violations have been made first of the authorities of the brigade commander and his competencies and the military police unit was engaged in matters that did not come under the realm of military police assignments. And in my work, on countless occasions I had conflicts, conflicts of opinion with respect to the engagement of the military police contrary to the law, an inappropriate deployment. So because of this inappropriate engagement of the police, what happened was that many other problems arose. And instead of the police solving those problems, it was somewhere taking up their position, somewhere which wasn't their assignment. They were on the front somewhere. And I could explain this from numerous aspects telling you why this is quite inappropriate and not in order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So if I go back to my earlier question that I asked way before, when I drew the objection from the Prosecution, you never drafted or participated in drafting this particular part of the order, as you claim you should have and as the -- as the rules require; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right, yes. I did not participate in the drafting of this order. And with respect to intelligence security and the first point of the order, I did not provide my proposals or give my opinions in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But nonetheless you would agree with me, would you not, this is an order? You may not like it. You may not agree with it. But it's an order.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's an order drafted by your commanding officer; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you may disagree with it, as far as I understand all over the world in the army when an order is given, you salute and you carry it out. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, it's not up to you to decide whether you're going to disregard an order and disregard what the commander has -- has decided simply because you have a philosophical or a scientific difference as to how the military police should be used. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, once again you are understanding this in your own particular way. The use and deployment of the military police is not a philosophical approach or any other kind of approach. The deployment of the military police is defined by law, by the rules of service. And therefore, the commander, issuing an order of any kind of command of any kind, is duty-bound to expect the rules of service and to use the units as they should be used, in combat actions and on all other occasions likewise. It is my duty, Mr. Karnavas, in cases of that kind - that is to say, if the commander to whom I am proposing something, proposing the use of the unit in come place with the rules and regulations and he rejects it, he did not accept it as a suggestion or proposal on my part, then he bears the responsibility for all the possible consequences that might arise through the inappropriate use of the unit, and it is my duty -- I am duty-bound through the chain of command and reporting to inform the superior command that the commander has inappropriately used a military police unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And did you do that in this instance? Call up and talk to Beara? You seem to have known him fairly -- fairly well in your prior dealings. Did you call him to -- to voice your objection?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that this order never reached me. It was not forwarded to me. I did not take part in it, and therefore I could not have reported back on it. Had I received it, I would have reported about -- on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I just want to be very clear on this, and I'll be as direct as possible. Are we to understand that during the attack on Srebrenica, before, during, and after - it took several days - you were unaware of any orders that had been drafted by the commander of the Bratunac Brigade which would have included tasks assigned to you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I would like to limit myself and say that we're discussing this particular order. And as regards this particular order, I am claiming that I did not write it, I did not receive it, I did not report back on the basis of it, and I did not act upon it. So when it comes to my actions and the actions of the military police platoon. And just to make this quite clear, in view of the fact that I did not know about the orders issued to the military police, I acted and prepared the military police platoon professionally speaking for complying with their military police tasks, which are the continuous tasks of a military police unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you also wore the hat of intelligence, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as the head of the intelligence service you were walking around for several days wondering what pray tell you might be doing during the operation on Srebrenica. You were clueless. You were without a clue of what to do. Is that what you're suggesting here today?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, intelligence work and the gathering of intelligence data is not a job that takes one, two, or three days, as you seem to be saying. This order was written on the 5th. On the corps command it was two or three days -- written two or three days prior to that. So the process of collecting intelligence data is a long one, a continuous ongoing one on the part of all the structures concerned, all the units concerned, and it's not something that can be accomplished in the space of three days. As chief of the Intelligence Department, I had a full perception of what was before me, and I knew full well all the details as far as my job was concerned, what I had to do with respect to the deployment of enemy forces, with their fortifications, their equipment in terms of weapons, and their general possibilities and capabilities, their weapons and ammunition, their possible axes of attack, their axes of withdrawal. I knew all that before this order was written. And just to give Their Honours an understanding of what I'm talking about, on my worksheet the intelligence organ -- the worksheet in my office, at all times the commander can come into my office and have a look at the deployment of forces, the situation on the previous day, and any possible changes in intelligence data on this working sheet compared to the previous day, for example, the map in fact. And they could read this in my intelligence diary as well. It was accessible to the commander on a daily basis, so he was free to peruse through it and look up any information he might need. Everything that my commander had was something that the superior command had access to, because it was my duty to send them my intelligence assessments and the evaluations with respect to the force, intentions, equipment of the enemy within the enclave, or rather, within the Srebrenica area. And that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Nikolic, I take it you were not aware that in Pribicevac it was a forward command post of the Bratunac Brigade at that time, the battle of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean you -- you think I didn't know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, are you saying that you through your intelligence knew what was already going to be in the order and therefore you had no need to read it or no need to ask what are the orders? Is that what you're suggesting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, that's a complete misstatement --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: A mischaracterisation of the evidence. Counsel is required to put his case during cross-examination. I'm not objecting to relevancy. I'm thinking something's coming here. But if -- I would object on the grounds he's not putting his case to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We got confused too, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Put your question directly to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what I understand, from the moment Srebrenica was attacked until after the fall of Srebrenica you never saw the order that was prepared by your commander. That's your answer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it not make -- does it not make sense that the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Battalions would need an order to know what exactly they're supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that can be seen from this order, that they did receive an order of this kind in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you claim never to have seen it, never to have read it; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, what I claimed was - and I've said it ten times - that I did not have this order, it was not sent to me, and I did not read it. I don't know the contents of this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say would that as the head of the intelligence sector and head of the security sector you made no efforts to see whether an order was ever issued, to see what might your role be in the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I have to say once again what the practice was. It's not up to me to invest any effort --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... As non-responsive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make an effort, sir, to find out whether there was an order; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way you ask your question, I can't give a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Nikolic, you were an intelligence officer. Part of that job requires you to gather intelligence, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to gather some intelligence as to whether an order existed? Like maybe ask somebody from the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Battalion or the commander, the chief of staff, somebody, anybody? Did you ever ask, "Is there an order? What are we doing?" Did you do anything?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, intelligence data does not mean collecting information as to the orders issued. That's not what it's about. That's not an intelligence piece of information and isn't gathered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you could look at paragraph 10, please, of the order. And we've identified it for identification purposes as D18/1. If you could look at that, please. And I believe it's -- it's under A, "Intelligence security." You will note --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, what's the number for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The identification, Your Honour, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think it's D17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. It's getting a little late. Not that that was a complaint, but just ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look at that. Now, it's on page -- well, these are not paginated, unfortunately. But you will note there is an area or there's -- there's some language dealing with POWs.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is a POW? A prisoner of war, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of collecting prisoners of war and looters the area of Pribicevac? Is that what you're referring to? But I don't have those letters and that abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's focus on that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this order does it not say that as long as this order exists, is in effect, that POWs from the Bratunac Brigade, that they gather, will be at Pribicevac? Does it not say this?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does say that, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, whether it's fortunately or unfortunately, that can be debated as a military academy. But right now in this particular order that's what it says; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that means that as long -- as long as this order is in effect all POWs captured by the Bratunac Brigade are to go to Pribicevac, not to some warehouse, not to some school, but over there. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it is written here in this order, that is correct. But I've tried to explain to you that what it says here is not my proposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I got that. I got that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the commander, Blagojevic, could have written whatever he wanted to write. And that's what he wrote and that is what it stands -- how it stands in the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's his prerogative, is it not, to write the order, even -- even after you make your recommendations, in the end it's up to him to decide whether to accept, modify, or come up with completely different proposals, because after all his name is on the order and at the end of the day he's going to be responsible.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, you're quite right in saying that. However, had I taken part in the writing or had I proposed this point in the order, it would never have been written in that fashion. And I can say with certainty that I would have adapted it to the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Just to pick up on that last point. Is that what you were doing on the 12th, when you -- when you indicated that you were the one that was suggesting to Popovic and Kosoric where to detain the people? You were adapting to the situation? Is that what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that 12th, I suggested to Popovic and Kosoric the facilities which were capable of taking in the assessed number of POWs who were in Potocari. And I also proposed facilities in which with a relatively small force we were -- would have been able to provide the physical security of those prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not a fact, sir, that this order was still in effect, especially as it pertained to you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That order was in effect only on paper. And as it was unknown to me, I was not able to act in conformity with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Especially the latter part, where it says "Apply Geneva Conventions in treatment of POW population." So you weren't aware that that's what the order had, you were free to treat the prisoners in whatever manner you, Momir Nikolic, saw fit at the time.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. I was not able to treat the prisoners in whatever manner I saw fit, and nobody ever in an order would write anything other than was written in this order. Do you really think that in an operation where 7.000 people were set aside, captured, and killed that somebody was adhering to the Geneva Conventions? Do you really believe that somebody adhered to the law, rules and regulations in an operation where so many were killed? First of all, they were captured, killed, and then buried, exhumed once again, buried again. Can you conceive of that, that somebody in an operation of that kind adhered to the Geneva Conventions? Nobody, Mr. Karnavas, adhered to the Geneva Conventions or the rules and regulations. Because had they, then the consequences of that particular operation would not have been a total of 7.000 people dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to you, Mr. Nikolic, this order was still in effect, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the order was in effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know you wish to go until 4.30. Is there any chance we might be able to knock off a little early? This would be a good time to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I think, you know, we could be very flexible to break or to resume at any time. If you believe that now is a good time to break, so we'll break now and we'll resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 26th day of September, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
